altar: The man who saw Jesus knelt and worshiped; at the Holy Qurbono the eyes of faith see the same Lord under the signs of bread and wine, and we bow before him.

2027-06-24.title: The Birth of John the Baptist · Thursday of the fifth week after Pentecost
readings: Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord
“His name is John”: the birth of the forerunner
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you, and imitate their faith
The faithful and wise servant whom the master finds at work
2027-06-24.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), which ends on 29 June. The Panchangam keeps today the Birth of John the Baptist (Yohannan Mamdana), with Hebrews 12:14–17 and Luke 1:57–66. It also keeps the memory of Cheppattu Philipose Ramban, with its own pair of readings (Hebrews 13:7–16; Matthew 24:45–51). A Ramban is a celibate monk-priest of the Syriac tradition; the Panchangam gives no further details of his life.
theo: The Church keeps the earthly birthday of very few saints. For most, she celebrates the day of their death, their birth into heaven. But she keeps the birth of Christ, the birth of his Mother, and the birth of John the Baptist, whom our tradition calls Yohannan Mamdana, John the Baptizer. St Augustine already remarked that the Church honours only two births with a solemn feast in his day, that of the Lord and that of John, because John's birth was itself part of the good news (Sermon 287, in substance). Before he was born, the angel told Zechariah: “even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.” And when the Mother of God, carrying the Lord in her womb, came to greet Elizabeth, “the child leaped in her womb.” The forerunner was sanctified by the presence of Christ before he saw the light of day. The feast falls six months before Christmas, as Luke's Gospel suggests, and Augustine noticed that after John's birth the days of the northern year begin to shorten, while after Christ's birth they begin to lengthen: the creation itself seems to repeat John's words, “He must increase, but I must decrease” (John 3:30; Augustine, Sermons on the Nativity of John, in substance).

St Luke tells the birth simply: “Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son. Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.” An old couple who had waited all their lives now hold a child, and the whole village shares their joy. Then comes the naming. “On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to name him Zechariah after his father.” In our own families it is the custom to name the first son after his grandfather, and everyone knows the quarrels that can follow when parents choose otherwise. Elizabeth breaks the custom: “No; he is to be called John.” The relatives object: “None of your relatives has this name.” They turn to Zechariah, who has been silent for nine months since he doubted the angel in the temple. “He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, ‘His name is John.’ And all of them were amazed.” The name was not the family's choice but God's, and it means that the Lord has shown favour. The moment Zechariah obeys, his silence ends: “Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.” The tongue that was tied by doubt is loosened by obedience, and its first words are praise.

The neighbours were filled with awe, and the news ran through the hill country of Judea. “All who heard them pondered them and said, ‘What then will this child become?’ For, indeed, the hand of the Lord was with him.” That question is asked over every cradle and at every baptismal font. This month, as the schools of Kerala reopen in the rain and children set out with new books and new uniforms, parents ask it again: what will this child become? John became a prophet of the desert, whose food was locusts and wild honey, a man of prayer and fasting who prepared a people for the Lord. It is fitting that his feast falls within the Apostles' Fast, for he prepared the Apostles too: St John's Gospel tells us that Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was first a disciple of John, and that it was John who pointed him to Jesus with the words “Look, here is the Lamb of God!” (John 1:36). The greatest of the prophets was the one who sent his own disciples away from himself to Christ.

The Epistle of the feast gives the shape of such a life: “Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.” Holiness is not a decoration for a few; it is the road by which anyone at all comes to see God. The letter warns against “a root of bitterness” (Hebrews 12:15) that springs up and defiles many, and against becoming “like Esau, an immoral and godless person, who sold his birthright for a single meal.” John never sold his birthright. He would not claim to be the Messiah when the crowds wanted him to, and he would not keep silent before Herod when silence would have saved his life. The fast trains us in the same freedom of heart: to refuse the single meal, the comfort, the flattery, for which we might trade our place as children of God. Today the Panchangam also remembers Cheppattu Philipose Ramban, and gives for his memory the words, “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” We know little of him beyond his name and his title, but the Church asks us to remember those monks, priests and teachers who handed on the faith in our land, and to be, like them and like John, faithful servants whom the Master finds at work when he comes.
outline: Opening
Ask: what did my parents hope I would become, and what does God hope I will become?
Point 1 · A birth that is good news
Why the Church celebrates the birthday of John, the forerunner sanctified before birth.
Point 2 · “His name is John”
God's name over the family's custom; Zechariah's obedience and his loosened tongue.
Point 3 · “What then will this child become?”
The prophet of the desert who prepared the Apostles and pointed them to the Lamb.
Point 4 · Holiness without which no one will see the Lord
Not selling our birthright for a single meal; the faithful leaders we remember.
Take-home line
“He must increase, but I must decrease.”
live: Let God name your plans (Luke 1:63)
Bring one decision you are making this week, about study, work or family, before God in prayer, and be ready to write “His name is John” where he asks.
Open your lips in praise (Luke 1:64)
Pray Zechariah's canticle, Luke 1:68–79, each morning until the feast of Sts Peter and Paul.
Pull up a root of bitterness (Hebrews 12:15)
Make peace this week with one relative with whom you have quarrelled.
2027-06-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Lamb of God, your forerunner John leaped for joy in his mother's womb at the greeting of your holy Mother, and his birth filled his parents and neighbours with gladness. As you loosened the tongue of Zechariah when he obeyed your word, open our lips to praise you. Give us the holiness without which no one will see you, keep us from every root of bitterness, and let us never sell our birthright for a single meal. Bless the children of our families as they begin a new school year, and let your hand be with them as it was with John. Through the prayers of John the Baptist, and in memory of your servant Philipose Ramban and of all who spoke your word to us, make us faithful servants, ready for your coming. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In many liturgies the Church repeats the words of John the Baptist as the Lamb of God is shown to us, and like John we point away from ourselves to the One who takes away the sin of the world and gives himself as our food.
conn: Called from the womb.

Isaiah 49:1 and Jeremiah 1:5 speak of prophets called and named before birth; Luke 1:15 and 1:41 show John filled with the Holy Spirit and leaping for joy in the womb at the greeting of the Mother of God.
The promised Elijah.
Malachi 4:5 promises the prophet Elijah before the day of the Lord; Jesus says of John in Matthew 11:14, “he is Elijah who is to come.”
From John to the Apostles.
John 1:35–42: Andrew and another disciple of John follow Jesus, and Andrew brings his brother Simon; the Apostles' Fast keeps the memory of those whom John helped prepare.
fathers: St Augustine

John is the voice, Christ is the Word: the voice passes once it has carried the word, but the Word remains for ever; John was a voice for a time, Christ was the Word in the beginning (Sermon 293, in substance).
St Bede the Venerable

Zechariah's tongue was loosed when he wrote the name, because the voice of praise is given back to those who obey; the grace that the name John signifies opened his mouth (Homilies on the Gospels, on the Nativity of John, in substance).
magis: Catechism 523

St John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor or forerunner, sent to prepare his way; “prophet of the Most High”, he surpasses all the prophets, of whom he is the last, and he inaugurates the Gospel, already from his mother's womb welcoming the coming of Christ and rejoicing in being the friend of the bridegroom (in substance).
Catechism 717

John was filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb by Christ himself, whom the Virgin Mary had just conceived by the Holy Spirit; Mary's visitation to Elizabeth thus became a visit from God to his people (in substance).
Lumen Gentium 40
All the faithful, of whatever rank or status, are called to the fullness of the Christian life and to the perfection of charity (in substance).

2027-06-25.title: Friday of the fifth week after Pentecost
readings: By faith Abraham offered up Isaac; by faith Isaac, Jacob and Joseph blessed the generations to come
“My teaching is not mine but his who sent me”; judge with right judgment
2027-06-25.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), which ends on 29 June. No commemoration is printed in the Panchangam today. A Friday of the fast.
2027-06-25.verse: Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.
theo: On this Friday of the Apostles' Fast, the Letter to the Hebrews takes us to the mountain where Abraham's faith was tried to the utmost: “By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to offer up his only son, of whom he had been told, ‘It is through Isaac that descendants shall be named for you.’” Everything God had promised seemed to hang on this one boy, and God asked for him. Abraham did not understand, but he trusted. The letter tells us what held him: “He considered the fact that God is able even to raise someone from the dead.” Abraham, whom Jews and Christians alike honour as our father in faith, believed that the God who gives life could give it back. The Fathers of the Church saw in Isaac, climbing the mountain with the wood on his shoulders, a figure of Christ carrying his cross; Origen told his hearers that Isaac bearing the wood for his own sacrifice shows us the Lord who carried the wood of the cross (Homilies on Genesis 8, in substance). On a Friday we remember that the Father did not withhold his only Son, and that the Son was truly raised from the dead.

The reading continues with three deathbeds and three blessings. “By faith Isaac invoked blessings for the future on Jacob and Esau. By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, ‘bowing in worship over the top of his staff.’ By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his burial.” These old men could not see the fulfilment of the promise, but they handed it on. Faith looks forward; it blesses those who will live after us. In our homes the elders still make the sign of the cross on the foreheads of children before a journey, an examination or the first day of school. This month, as the schools reopen, that small gesture is repeated in thousands of houses. It is not a superstition; it is the faith of Isaac and Jacob, a blessing given by those who believe that God will keep his promises to the next generation even when they are no longer here to see it.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches in the temple at the feast of Tabernacles, and his hearers are astonished: “How does this man have such learning, when he has never been taught?” Jesus does not boast of his learning. He points away from himself: “My teaching is not mine but his who sent me. Anyone who resolves to do the will of God will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I am speaking on my own.” Here is a key to the life of faith: understanding comes to those who obey. St Augustine, commenting on these words, told his people that if they did not yet understand, they should believe and do the will of God, for understanding is the reward of faith (Tractates on John 29, in substance). When the evangelist writes “the Jews” here, he means the religious authorities in Jerusalem who opposed Jesus, not a whole people; the Church teaches that the Jewish people as such may not be blamed for the death of Christ (Catechism 597). Jesus then defends his healing of a man on the sabbath and ends with a word for every age: “Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.” The fast is a time to cleanse our judgements too: to stop judging others by their clothes, their caste, their accent or their past, and to look, as God does, at the heart.
outline: Opening
Ask: what blessing have I received from those before me, and what blessing will I hand on?
Point 1 · Faith that offers
Abraham on the mountain: trust in the God who can raise the dead.
Point 2 · Faith that blesses
Isaac, Jacob and Joseph hand on the promise; the sign of the cross on a child's forehead.
Point 3 · Right judgment
The teaching that comes from the Father, understood by those who do his will; not judging by appearances.
Take-home line
“Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.”
live: Bless the next generation (Hebrews 11:20–21)
Make the sign of the cross on the forehead of a child, a grandchild or a godchild this week, and pray for them by name.
Judge with right judgment (John 7:24)
Catch yourself the next time you judge someone by appearance, and say a prayer for that person instead.
2027-06-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, on this Friday we remember that the Father did not withhold you, his only Son, but gave you up for us all, and raised you from the dead. Give us the faith of Abraham, who trusted when he did not understand, and the faith of Isaac, Jacob and Joseph, who blessed the generations to come. Teach us to do the will of the Father, so that we may know that your teaching is from God. Cleanse our hearts of rash and proud judgements, and let us look on others as you look on them. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Abraham went up the mountain trusting that God would provide; at the Holy Qurbono the Lamb whom God provided is offered, and the sacrifice of Calvary is made present for us on the altar.

2027-06-26.title: Saturday of the fifth week after Pentecost
readings: Your gift is a fragrant offering; my God will fully satisfy every need of yours
“Whoever is from God hears the words of God”
2027-06-26.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), which ends on 29 June. No commemoration is printed in the Panchangam today. Tomorrow, the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost, is Seminary Day, with a collection for the Major Seminary of our Church, and the memory of Yakob Mar Theophilos (1956).
2027-06-26.verse: And my God will fully satisfy every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
theo: St Paul ends his letter to the Philippians with a thank-you. “You Philippians indeed know that in the early days of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving, except you alone. For even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent me help for my needs more than once.” The church at Philippi was poor and often persecuted, yet it was the one community that kept on supporting the apostle as he carried the gospel from town to town. Paul is careful about how he thanks them: “Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the profit that accumulates to your account.” What delights him is not the money but what their giving does to them; every gift for the gospel is written in God's book to their credit. Tomorrow the Panchangam keeps Seminary Day, and the offerings of the Holy Qurbono will go to the Major Seminary of our Church, where young men are formed to be priests. In the Apostles' Fast, when we remember the first men Christ sent, it is fitting that we support those who are being prepared to be sent today. The parish that gives to the seminary is doing exactly what the Philippians did for Paul: sharing in the gospel by giving and receiving.

Paul then describes their gift in the language of worship: “I have been paid in full and have more than enough; I am fully satisfied, now that I have received from Epaphroditus the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God.” A gift for the poor or for the mission is not only an act of kindness; it rises to God like the incense of the temple. And it never leaves the giver poorer in the end: “And my God will fully satisfy every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus. To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.” Paul does not promise that the Philippians will become wealthy. He promises that God, who is rich beyond measure, will not let them lack what they truly need. A family that shares even from a small income discovers this again and again, and that discovery is itself a reason to give glory to God.

The Gospel brings us into one of the sharpest disputes in St John's Gospel. Jesus is speaking with listeners who, a few verses earlier, are said to be looking for an opportunity to kill him, and he tells them: “If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and now I am here.” Then he speaks plainly of the devil: “He was a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks according to his own nature, for he is a liar and the father of lies.” These words were spoken to particular opponents at a particular moment; the Church has always taught that they may not be turned against the Jewish people as a whole (Nostra Aetate 4; Catechism 597). Their warning is for us. From the first lie in the garden, the enemy has worked through falsehood. St Augustine observed that whoever tells a lie speaks from what is his own, while whoever speaks the truth speaks from God, the source of all truth (Tractates on John 42, in substance). In an age of rumours forwarded from phone to phone, the fast of the tongue matters as much as the fast of the stomach: no lie, no gossip, no message passed on without knowing it is true. “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.” Let us belong to God by listening to his word and by speaking only what is true.
outline: Opening
Ask: whose words do I listen to most, and do my own words carry the truth?
Point 1 · Partners in the gospel
The poor church of Philippi that kept on supporting Paul; Seminary Day tomorrow.
Point 2 · A fragrant offering
A gift for the gospel rises to God like incense; God supplies every need.
Point 3 · Whoever is from God hears
The father of lies and the children of truth; the fast of the tongue.
Take-home line
“Whoever is from God hears the words of God.”
live: Share in the gospel (Philippians 4:15)
Give generously at tomorrow's Seminary Day collection, and pray by name for a seminarian or a young priest you know.
Keep the fast of the tongue (John 8:44–47)
For the rest of the Apostles' Fast, forward no message and repeat no story unless you know it is true and kind.
2027-06-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came from the Father and you speak the truth. Make us children of God who hear your words and love you. Keep us from every lie, from gossip and from rumours that wound our neighbours, and let our speech be true and kind. Bless all who share in the work of the gospel by their gifts, and make their offering a fragrant sacrifice, pleasing to the Father. Bless our Major Seminary, its teachers and its students, and send faithful labourers into your harvest. According to the riches of your glory, supply every need of our families. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The gifts we bring to the altar rise to God as a fragrant offering, and in the Holy Qurbono Christ joins them to his own perfect sacrifice, the offering that is fully pleasing to the Father.

2027-06-28.title: Monday of the sixth week after Pentecost · Mar Irenaeus
readings: Avoid wrangling over words; a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth
“You did not choose me but I chose you”: fruit that will last
2027-06-28.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. Today is the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), which ends tomorrow with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul. The Panchangam remembers Mar Irenaeus (St Irenaeus of Lyons, bishop, died about 202) and keeps the name day of Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios.
2027-06-28.verse: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved by him, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth.
theo: This is the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast. Tomorrow we keep the feast of Sts Peter and Paul and the fast comes to an end. Today St Paul, writing from prison to his young disciple Timothy, gives advice that every teacher of the faith needs: “Remind them of this, and warn them before God that they are to avoid wrangling over words, which does no good but only ruins those who are listening.” Paul is not against careful thought; he is against the quarrelsome spirit that turns the word of God into a battlefield for pride. Then he gives the positive picture: “Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved by him, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth. Avoid profane chatter, for it will lead people into more and more impiety.” The word translated “rightly explaining” describes cutting a straight road or a straight furrow: the teacher's task is to lay the word of truth out straight, so that others can walk on it. Every catechist, every parent who teaches a child to pray, every preacher on Sunday, is called to be such a worker.

The Panchangam today remembers a bishop who did exactly that: Mar Irenaeus, St Irenaeus of Lyons. He was born in Asia Minor in the second century, and as a young man he listened to St Polycarp of Smyrna, who had himself known the Apostle John. Years later Irenaeus wrote to a friend that he could still describe the place where Polycarp sat and talked, and how he told of his conversations with John and with others who had seen the Lord (in Eusebius, Church History 5.20, in substance). Irenaeus went to Gaul, served as a priest in Lyons and, after the martyrdom of Bishop Pothinus in the persecution of 177, became bishop there. In his day groups called Gnostics were wrangling over secret words and hidden teachings, claiming a knowledge higher than the faith of ordinary Christians. Against them Irenaeus wrote his great work Against Heresies. He did not answer with clever speculation; he pointed to the faith handed down openly from the Apostles in the churches through the succession of bishops, and above all to the Church of Rome, which he described as founded and organized by the two most glorious apostles, Peter and Paul (Against Heresies 3.3.2, in substance), the Apostles whose feast we keep tomorrow.

His name means peaceful, and the historian Eusebius remarked that he lived up to it, for when a dispute about the date of Easter threatened to divide the churches, Irenaeus wrote to the Bishop of Rome urging patience and peace (Church History 5.24, in substance). In 2022 Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church with the title Doctor of Unity. Irenaeus also left us one of the most beautiful sayings of the early Church: the glory of God is a human being fully alive, and the life of a human being is the vision of God (Against Heresies 4.20.7, in substance). Tradition honours him as a martyr; he died around the year 202. Today too the Panchangam keeps the name day of Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios. In our tradition a bishop receives a new name at his ordination, and the feast of the saint whose name he bears is kept as his name day. We pray today that he may be, like his patron, a teacher of the true faith and a servant of unity.

The Gospel shows where all this begins. Jesus says to the Apostles: “You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last, so that the Father will give you whatever you ask him in my name. I am giving you these commands so that you may love one another.” The Apostles did not apply for the job; they were chosen. The fruit they bore has lasted twenty centuries: John taught Polycarp, Polycarp taught Irenaeus, and the faith came down the generations, through the Apostle Thomas and his successors, to our own land and our own parish. The fruit that lasts is not wrangling but love. On this last day of the fast, let us thank God for those who handed on the faith to us, ask for the grace to explain it straight and live it with love, and prepare our hearts for tomorrow's feast of the two Apostles on whom, as Irenaeus taught, the Church of Rome was founded.
outline: Opening
Ask: when I speak about my faith, do I build up or do I quarrel?
Point 1 · Workers with no need to be ashamed
Avoid wrangling over words; lay the word of truth out straight.
Point 2 · Mar Irenaeus, teacher of the apostolic faith
From John to Polycarp to Irenaeus; the faith handed down in the Church, founded on Peter and Paul.
Point 3 · The peacemaker
A bishop who lived up to his name; the glory of God is a human being fully alive.
Point 4 · Chosen to bear lasting fruit
The Apostles chosen by Christ, the fruit of love that lasts.
Take-home line
“You did not choose me but I chose you.”
live: Explain the word straight (2 Timothy 2:15)
Read tomorrow's Gospel of the feast (John 21:15–19) tonight and explain it in simple words to one member of your family.
Avoid wrangling (2 Timothy 2:14)
Refuse to join one argument about religion or the Church this week, online or at home, that only wounds; say a prayer for unity instead.
Bear fruit in love (John 15:17)
Thank by name someone who handed on the faith to you, by a call, a visit or a prayer.
2027-06-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you chose your Apostles and appointed them to go and bear fruit that will last. Through the prayers of Mar Irenaeus, who received the faith from those who knew your Apostles and defended it with patience and peace, keep your Church in the true faith handed down to us. Make us workers who have no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth, and keep us from wrangling over words and from idle talk. Bless our bishop Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day, and all the shepherds of your Church. As the Apostles' Fast ends, prepare our hearts to celebrate Sts Peter and Paul, and let us bear the fruit of love. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Irenaeus taught that the bread over which God's name is invoked is no longer common bread but the Eucharist; at every Holy Qurbono the faith of the Apostles is handed on, and the fruit that lasts is given to us as food.
conn: A chain of faithful teachers.

2 Timothy 2:2: “what you have heard from me through many witnesses entrust to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well”; Irenaeus received the faith from Polycarp, who had known the Apostle John.
Chosen to bear fruit.
John 15:16 describes the choice of the Apostles; the Apostles' Fast, which ends tomorrow, remembers their mission, and Irenaeus is one of its lasting fruits.
Founded on Peter and Paul.
Irenaeus wrote that the Church of Rome was founded and organized by Peter and Paul (Against Heresies 3.3.2); their feast is kept tomorrow, 29 June.
fathers: St Irenaeus of Lyons

The Church, though spread throughout the whole world, carefully preserves the one faith received from the Apostles and their disciples, as if she lived in one house and had one soul and one mouth (Against Heresies 1.10.2, in substance).
Eusebius of Caesarea
Irenaeus was well named, for in name and in deed he was a peacemaker, pleading for the peace of the churches (Church History 5.24, in substance).
St Augustine

Jesus says: You did not choose me; this is grace that cannot be spoken, for what were we before Christ chose us, if not sinners? He chose us not because we were good, but to make us good (Tractates on John 86, in substance).
magis: Catechism 173–174

Irenaeus taught that the Church, scattered through the whole world, guards the faith received from the Apostles as one family, with one heart and one voice; so the Church's message is true and solid, showing one way of salvation in all the world (in substance).
Catechism 834

Particular Churches are fully catholic through their communion with the Church of Rome, which presides in charity; Irenaeus taught that with this Church, because of its superior origin, all the Churches must agree (in substance).
Catechism 294
The glory of God consists in the realization of his goodness; as Irenaeus said, the glory of God is a human being fully alive, and the life of a human being is the vision of God (in substance).

2027-06-30.title: The Twelve Apostles · Wednesday of the sixth week after Pentecost
readings: Servants of God: as having nothing, and yet possessing everything
He appointed twelve, to be with him and to be sent out to proclaim the message
2027-06-30.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps today the commemoration of the Twelve Apostles, the day after the feast of Sts Peter and Paul, with which the Apostles' Fast ended. On Saturday, 3 July, the Church keeps the Dukhrono of Mar Thoma Shleeha, the Apostle of India.
2027-06-30.verse: And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message,
theo: Yesterday the Church celebrated the two great pillars, Peter and Paul, and the Apostles' Fast came to an end. Today, as if gathering the whole family together after the feast, she remembers all the Twelve. St Mark tells how it began: “He went up the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him.” St Luke adds that before choosing them Jesus “spent the night in prayer to God” (Luke 6:12). The call of the Apostles was born in the prayer of the Son to the Father, and it came from his choice, not theirs. The mountain recalls Sinai, where God formed Israel as his people, and the number twelve recalls the twelve tribes: in choosing the Twelve, Jesus was gathering a renewed people of God, the Church. The Book of Revelation sees the end of the story in the heavenly city: “And the wall of the city has twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb” (Revelation 21:14). Every one of us who believes stands on those foundations.

Mark tells us why they were chosen: “And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message, and to have authority to cast out demons.” There are two movements here, and their order matters. First, to be with him; then, to be sent. No one can be sent who has not first been with Jesus, at table, on the road, in prayer, at the foot of the cross. And whoever has truly been with him cannot keep him to himself. Then Mark gives the names, and what a mixture they are: Simon, to whom Jesus gave the name Peter; James and John, the fiery brothers he called Sons of Thunder; Andrew and Philip; Bartholomew, whom our calendar remembered as Mar Barthulmai on 11 June; Matthew, the tax collector; Thomas, who brought the gospel to our land and whose Dukhrono we keep on Saturday; James son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus, remembered as Mar Yuda Thaddai on 19 June; Simon the Cananaean; and Judas Iscariot, “who betrayed him.” Fishermen and a tax collector, quiet men and hot-tempered ones: Jesus did not choose them because they were alike, but made them one around himself. The sad last name reminds us that even one who has been close to the Lord can fall away, and the Church later chose Matthias to take his place among the Twelve.

In the Epistle, St Paul, who was not one of the Twelve but was called by the risen Lord, describes the apostolic life from the inside. “As we work together with him, we urge you also not to accept the grace of God in vain. For he says, ‘At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.’ See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!” The fast is over, but the acceptable time is not; it is always now. Then Paul lists what the work of an apostle cost him: “through great endurance, in afflictions, hardships, calamities, beatings, imprisonments, riots, labors, sleepless nights, hunger.” Tradition tells that almost all of the Twelve gave their lives for Christ. Yet Paul ends with a song of paradoxes: “as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.” St John Chrysostom, who loved Paul dearly, said that the apostles had no house of their own, yet every house of the faithful was open to them, and that this is what it means to have nothing and possess everything (Homilies on Second Corinthians, in substance).

The Church that the Twelve founded is still apostolic. The bishops, gathered around the successor of Peter, are the successors of the Apostles, and the faith we profess is the faith they preached. Our own Church treasures the apostolic faith brought to India by Mar Thoma Shleeha, and lives it in full communion with the Bishop of Rome. But to be apostolic is not only a matter of history and of bishops. Every baptized Christian is called, like the Twelve, to be with Jesus and to be sent. To be with him in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono; to be sent to the office, the field, the classroom and the hospital ward, carrying the message. The fast has ended; the mission has not. Today, at the turning of the month, let us thank God for the Twelve, ask their prayers, and offer ourselves again to be with the Lord and to go where he sends us.
outline: Opening
Ask: how much time do I spend with Jesus, and where is he sending me?
Point 1 · Called up the mountain
Chosen after a night of prayer; the twelve foundations of the new people of God.
Point 2 · To be with him
The first purpose of the call: friendship and prayer.
Point 3 · To be sent
Twelve very different men, made one and sent; Thomas who came to our land.
Point 4 · Having nothing, possessing everything
The cost and the joy of the apostolic life; now is the acceptable time.
Take-home line
“to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message”
live: Be with him (Mark 3:14)
Set aside fifteen minutes each day this week for silent prayer with the Gospel, as the first part of your mission.
Be sent (Mark 3:14)
Choose one person who does not know Christ or has drifted away, and share a word of faith or an invitation with them before the Dukhrono of St Thomas on Saturday.
Do not receive grace in vain (2 Corinthians 6:1)
Keep one good habit from the Apostles' Fast, a prayer, a small fast or an act of almsgiving, for the rest of the year.
2027-06-30.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, after a night of prayer you called to yourself those whom you wanted, and you appointed the Twelve to be with you and to be sent out to proclaim your message. We thank you for your holy Apostles, the foundations of your Church, and especially for Mar Thoma Shleeha, who brought your gospel to our land. Through their prayers keep us in the apostolic faith and in communion with the successor of Peter. Draw us to be with you in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono, and send us out as your witnesses. When the work is hard, let us be sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing and yet possessing everything in you. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The Twelve were with Jesus at the Last Supper, when he said, Do this in remembrance of me; at every Holy Qurbono the Church, built on the Apostles, does what he commanded them, and the Lord is again with his own.
conn: Chosen in prayer.
Luke 6:12–13: Jesus spent the night in prayer on the mountain, and when day came he chose twelve and named them apostles; Mark 3:13–19 is today's account of the same call.
The twelve foundations.

Revelation 21:14: the wall of the heavenly city has twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb; Ephesians 2:20 speaks of the household of God built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets.
The Twelve made whole again.
Acts 1:26: after the fall of Judas the lot fell on Matthias, and he was added to the eleven apostles; the apostolic ministry continues in the Church.
fathers: St Clement of Rome

The apostles received the gospel for us from the Lord Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ was sent from God; so Christ is from God and the apostles are from Christ. Preaching in country and town, they appointed their first converts, after testing them by the Spirit, to be bishops and deacons of those who would believe (Letter to the Corinthians 42, in substance).
St John Chrysostom

The apostles had nothing, yet they possessed everything: they had no house, yet the houses of all the faithful were open to them; they owned nothing, yet they lacked nothing, because they possessed Christ (Homilies on Second Corinthians, in substance).
magis: Catechism 858

Jesus is the Father's emissary. From the beginning of his ministry he called to him those whom he desired and appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out to preach; from then on they would be his emissaries, and in them Christ continues his own mission (in substance).
Catechism 765

The Lord Jesus endowed his community with a structure that will remain until the Kingdom is fully achieved: the choice of the Twelve with Peter as their head; representing the twelve tribes of Israel, they are the foundation stones of the new Jerusalem (in substance).
Lumen Gentium 20
By divine institution the bishops have succeeded to the place of the apostles as shepherds of the Church, so that whoever hears them hears Christ (in substance).

quick: “I am the bread of life”: whoever comes to Jesus will never hunger.
The Twelve are sent two by two to preach repentance and heal.
“But if not”: faith that will not worship idols whatever happens.
2027-06-06.action: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with someone from your family.
2027-06-06.question: Do I trust God even when he does not answer as I want?
2027-06-06.special: Third Sunday after Pentecost. This week (11 June): anniversary of the erection of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy in 1932.
illus: An illustration

In 1930 Mar Ivanios and a few companions entered communion with the Catholic Church, leaving buildings and properties behind. They had little, but went out like the apostles, two by two. In 1932 the Syro-Malankara hierarchy was erected. Faith first, whatever it costs.

family.explain: Three young men would not bow down to a golden statue, even when the king threatened them with fire. They loved God more than anything!
family.intention: We pray for courage to put God first always.
family.ask: Ask: “What ‘golden statues’ tempt us to put them before God?”

kidsaint: St Antony of Padua (13 June)

A Franciscan priest who preached so well that people said even the fish came to listen! He loved the poor, and people still give “St Antony's bread” to the hungry. Lesson: share your bread as Jesus shares himself.
term: Two by two
Jesus sent the apostles in pairs (Mark 6:7; Luke 10:1): for support, for witness (two witnesses make a testimony), and as a sign that mission is done in communion, not alone.
termMore: On 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI, by the bull Christo Pastorum Principi, erected the Syro-Malankara hierarchy with the Archeparchy of Trivandrum and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla. In 2005 the Church was raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church.

quick: “You give them something to eat”: Christ feeds his people through his disciples.
“Whoever wants to be first must be servant of all.”
God chooses unexpected instruments and forms them for service.
2027-06-20.action: Pray each day this week for the seminarians of your eparchy.
2027-06-20.question: What are my “five loaves” that Jesus wants me to offer?
2027-06-20.special: Fifth Sunday after Pentecost. Apostles' Fast under way.
illus: An illustration
A Kerala mother packs a tiffin of rice and fish for her son leaving for the seminary. Years later he holds up the Bread of Life at the altar. Her small gift became part of something far greater.

family.explain: A boy's small lunch of five loaves and two fish fed thousands when Jesus blessed it. When we give what we have, Jesus can do great things.
family.intention: We pray for priests and seminarians.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can we give to Jesus this week?”

catechism: The multiplication of loaves and the Eucharist.
The priest acts in the person of Christ.
kidsaint: St John Vianney

A priest who found studying very hard and almost failed the seminary. But he loved God so much that people came from all over France to confess to him in the little village of Ars. He is patron of parish priests. Lesson: God can use anyone who loves him.
term: Sleehanombu
The Apostles' Fast, kept in the Syro-Malankara Church before the feast of Sts Peter and Paul (29 June). It prepares the faithful to honour the apostles, the foundation of the Church.
termMore: A “seed-bed” (Latin seminarium) where candidates for the priesthood are formed in prayer, study, community life and pastoral service. St Mary's Malankara Major Seminary, Trivandrum, was established in 1989.

quick: The Good Shepherd searches for the lost one; heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
The Church and the family are one body: every member matters.
Forgive seven times a day, and pray “Increase our faith!”
2027-06-27.action: Contact someone in your family or parish who has drifted from the Church.
2027-06-27.question: Who is the “lost sheep” God is asking me to seek?
2027-06-27.special: Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. Seminary Day; collection for the Major Seminary. Memory of Yakob Mar Theophilos (1956). Check your eparchy's circular. The Apostles' Fast ends on Tuesday.
illus: An illustration

A Kerala grandmother lit the evening lamp every day for a grandson who had stopped coming to church, and prayed the Rosary for him. Years later he came back for her funeral and stayed. The shepherd had been searching through her.

family.explain: Jesus is like a shepherd who goes looking for one lost sheep, and is so happy when he finds it that he carries it home on his shoulders.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family welcome someone who feels left out?”

kidsaint: Sts Louis and Zélie Martin

A watchmaker and a lace-maker in France who prayed together with their five daughters every day. One of them became St Thérèse of the Child Jesus. They were canonised together in 2015. Lesson: a family that prays together grows saints.
term: The Seventy-two Disciples
Besides the Twelve, Jesus sent seventy-two others ahead of him two by two (Luke 10:1). The Syriac tradition honours them on a Sunday after Pentecost as the wider circle of missionaries.
termMore: Holy incense (Exodus 30:34–38) is used abundantly in the West Syriac liturgy. Its sweet smoke rising symbolises prayer ascending to God (Psalm 141:2) and the fragrance of Christ's sacrifice.

quick: “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church.”
“Do you love me?… Feed my sheep”: authority born of mercy and love.
“I have fought the good fight… I have kept the faith.”
2027-06-29.action: Pray today for Pope Leo XIV and our Major Archbishop.
2027-06-29.question: If Jesus asked me “Do you love me?”, what would my life answer?
2027-06-29.special: Sts Peter and Paul (Tuesday): Holy Qurbono for the people; end of the Apostles' Fast.
illus: An illustration

In Rome, under the high altar of St Peter's Basilica, archaeologists found the grave of a man venerated since the first century. Pope Paul VI announced in 1968 that the relics of St Peter had been identified. The Church is literally built on the fisherman.

family.explain: Peter had said three times that he did not know Jesus. Jesus forgave him by asking three times: “Do you love me?” Then he made Peter the shepherd of his people.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, our bishops and priests.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show Jesus that we love him this week?”

kidsaint: Sts Peter and Paul

Peter was a fisherman who sometimes got things wrong, but he loved Jesus. Paul once fought against Christians, but Jesus changed his heart. Both became great apostles and gave their lives for Jesus in Rome. Lesson: Jesus can change anyone who says yes to him.
term: Primacy of Peter

The special office Christ gave to Peter as the rock of the Church, the holder of the keys and the shepherd of the flock (Matthew 16; John 21), continued in the Bishop of Rome. The Catholic Eastern Churches, including the Syro-Malankara Church, are in full communion with him.
termMore: The Apostles' Fast concludes on this feast. Fasting prepares us to honour the apostles who handed on the faith we received.

quick: Before sending the seventy, Jesus asks them to pray for laborers.
“Peace to this house!”: the first word of the messenger.
“Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
2027-06-13.action: Pray each day this week for one priest and for one young person who may be called.
2027-06-13.question: Is my joy in what I achieve for God, or in belonging to him?
2027-06-13.special: Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. St Antony of Padua. Announce the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), 16–29 June.
illus: An illustration

An old catechist in a hill parish taught Sunday school for forty years. Few of his pupils remembered his lessons word for word. But when one of them was ordained a priest, the first person he blessed after his parents was the old man, who wept and said: “I only prayed and taught. The Lord of the harvest did the rest.”

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends in pairs to visit towns. They were to say “Peace to this house!”, heal the sick and tell people that God's kingdom was near.
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters and catechists, and for new vocations from our parish.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family bring peace to a house we visit this week?”

kidsaint: St Antony of Padua (13 June)

Born in Lisbon in Portugal, he first became an Augustinian canon. When he saw the bodies of Franciscan friars martyred in Morocco brought home, he joined the Franciscans and wanted to be a missionary. God led him instead to preach in Italy and France, and crowds came to hear him. He died near Padua in 1231 and is a Doctor of the Church. Lesson: go where God sends you, and speak his word with love.
term: Shleeha Nombu

The Apostles' Fast. In the Syro-Malankara Church it is kept from 16 June to 29 June, ending with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul. The faithful pray, fast and give alms, asking for the apostolic spirit.
termMore: A number of fullness in the Bible: seventy elders shared the spirit of Moses (Numbers 11:16–25), and the list of nations in Genesis 10 has seventy (seventy-two in the Greek). The seventy disciples stand for the mission to every nation.

quick: St Paul calls the Church the household of God, the pillar and bulwark of the truth.
An early hymn tells the whole mystery of Christ: revealed in flesh, vindicated in spirit, taken up in glory.
Asked “Who are you?”, Jesus says that when he is lifted up they will know that “I am he”; St Justin searched for the truth and died for Christ about the year 165.
2027-06-01.action: Pray today for one student and one teacher you know, as schools reopen.
2027-06-01.question: In my own search for meaning, have I let Jesus answer the question “Who are you?”

family.explain: People asked Jesus: who are you? Jesus said they would understand when he was lifted up, which means on the Cross. On the Cross we see how much Jesus loves us and how he always does what his Father wants. Long ago a young man called Justin wanted to know the truth. He asked many clever teachers, but he found the answer only when he read the Bible and met Jesus. He loved Jesus so much that he gave his life for him.
family.intention: We pray for all the children and teachers starting a new school year, that they may learn well and grow in wisdom.
family.ask: Ask: “If someone asked me ‘Who is Jesus?’, what would I say?”

illus: An illustration

A retired mathematics teacher in a parish near Mavelikara kept a small exercise book from his first year of teaching, 1971. In it he had written the names of every student, and beside each name a short prayer. Every June, when the school bell rang again after the vacation, he would take it out and pray through the names, though most of those students were now grandparents. A young teacher once asked him why. He said: when I was young I thought I was only teaching sums; later I understood that I was looking after souls who were looking for the truth, and the truth is a person. Then he showed her the first page, where he had copied a line from 1 Timothy: the church of the living God, the pillar and bulwark of the truth.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the truth that every heart is looking for. As St Justin sought you and found you, let us find you in your word and in your Church. Amen.
share: The household of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and bulwark of the truth (1 Timothy 3:15). Where has the Church held up the truth for me when I was confused?
They said to him, “Who are you?” (John 8:25). How would I answer that question about Jesus in my own words?
When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). When did the Cross teach me who Jesus is?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the truth; lead us to you.
interc: For the Church, the household of God, that she may always hold up the truth with courage and with love.
For children, students and teachers returning to schools and colleges, that they may grow in knowledge and in wisdom.
For those who search for meaning in many places, that they may meet Christ, as St Justin did.
For Christians who suffer for their faith, that like St Justin and his companions they may stand firm.
For our farmers and for all who wait for the monsoon rains, that the rains may be good and bring no harm.
pm.close: Father, through St Justin you showed that the truth sought by the mind is found in your Son, lifted up on the Cross. Keep us in your household, faithful to the truth, and give us courage to confess Christ before all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Apology (അപ്പോളജി)

From the Greek word apologia, a speech in defence, as in a court of law. It does not mean saying sorry. St Justin's two Apologies were written to the Roman emperors to defend the Christians against false charges and to explain what they believed and how they worshipped. From this word comes apologetics, the reasoned defence of the faith.
kidsaint: St Justin and the old man by the sea

Justin was a clever young man who wanted to know the truth about God. He went to one teacher after another. One asked for money first, one wanted him to learn music and geometry before anything else, one did not care about God at all. One day, walking alone by the sea, Justin met an old man who told him to read the prophets in the Bible, because they spoke about Jesus. Justin read them and his heart was set on fire. He became a Christian and taught others for the rest of his life, and in the end he gave his life for Jesus. Lesson: keep asking questions, and look for the answers in Jesus.

quick: To those who are perishing the message of the cross is foolishness; to those being saved it is the power of God.
Christ crucified is the power of God and the wisdom of God; God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom.
The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that grows into a tree and like yeast that leavens a great mass of flour.
2027-06-02.action: Do one small good deed in secret today and leave the growth to God.
2027-06-02.question: Where am I impatient for quick, visible results instead of trusting God's hidden way of working?

family.explain: Jesus told two little stories. A mustard seed is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice, but it grows into a big plant where birds can build nests. A little yeast mixed into a big bowl of flour makes the whole dough rise, like the dough for appam. God's kingdom grows like that: from small beginnings, quietly, from inside. Every small kind thing we do is like a seed or a pinch of yeast.
family.intention: We pray for our farmers who are planting in this rainy season, and for every small good work in our family to grow.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small seed of kindness I can plant tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Kollam, a widow began in the 1990s to keep a few rupees aside every week in a tin on her kitchen shelf. When the tin was full she would buy notebooks and pencils for one child in the colony who could not afford them. She never spoke about it. Years later, at her funeral, the parish priest was surprised to see a group of young men and women he did not know standing near the back: a nurse, two teachers, an engineer, a police constable. They had all, as children, received their first notebooks from her tin. One of them said: it was such a small thing; it was the reason I stayed in school. The priest went home and read again the parable of the mustard seed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your Cross is the power of God. Sow your word in our hearts like a seed and let it grow, quietly and surely, by your Spirit. Amen.
share: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God (1 Corinthians 1:18). When has the Cross been power for me?
It is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in the garden; it grew and became a tree (Luke 13:19). What small beginning in my life did God make grow?
It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened (Luke 13:21). Where can I be a little yeast this week?
pm.resp: Lord, let your kingdom grow in us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim Christ crucified with courage, even when the world calls it foolishness.
For preachers and teachers of the faith, that they may trust the power of the Cross more than their own cleverness.
For our farmers and all who work the land in this monsoon season, that their sowing may be blessed.
For all who feel that their good efforts are too small to matter, that they may be encouraged.
For our parish, that the Gospel may work in us like yeast, quietly changing our homes and our town.
pm.close: Father, in the foolishness of the Cross you have shown your wisdom, and in small seeds you prepare a great harvest. Give us faith to trust your hidden ways and patience to wait for your growth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Those who believe are the descendants of Abraham; in him all the Gentiles are blessed.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
An unclean spirit that finds its old house swept but empty returns with seven worse spirits.
2027-06-03.action: Replace one empty or wasted hour today with prayer, reading Scripture or helping someone.
2027-06-03.question: Is my heart a swept but empty house, or a home where the Holy Spirit lives?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a house that was swept clean, but nobody lived in it. So a bad spirit came back and brought seven friends! Jesus is teaching us that it is not enough to stop doing bad things. We must fill our hearts with good things: prayer, kindness, helping, the love of Jesus. When the Holy Spirit lives in our hearts, there is no room for bad things to come back.
family.intention: We pray that the Holy Spirit may live in our home and fill it with peace and love.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing can I put in my heart this week instead of something bad I want to stop doing?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a parish near Pathanamthitta came back from a rehabilitation centre after six months, sober at last. His counsellor had told him one thing on the day he left: the bottle will not be your problem now, the empty evenings will be. For the first weeks he sat at home after work and felt the old pull. Then the parish youth group asked him to help with the evening tuition classes they ran for children in the colony. He went, at first only to fill the time. Two years later he was running the classes. When the vicar asked him what had kept him sober, he said: I did not only sweep the house, Father; I let someone move in.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, fill our hearts. Do not let them be swept and empty, but make your home in us. Amen.
share: Those who believe are blessed with Abraham who believed (Galatians 3:9). Where has my faith brought blessing to others?
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us (Galatians 3:13). What does it mean to me that Christ took my place?
When it comes, it finds it swept and put in order (Luke 11:25). What have I put in the place of the evil I gave up?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, live in us.
interc: For the Church, that all the baptized may live by faith and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
For those struggling to give up addictions or sinful habits, that they may find good things to fill their lives and good friends to walk with them.
For the Jewish people, the children of Abraham, to whom God first spoke, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For young people facing temptation, that they may have the courage of the martyrs of Uganda.
For our families, that our homes may be filled with prayer and with the peace of the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, through the Cross of your Son you have swept us clean, and through faith you give us the promise of the Spirit. Do not let our hearts stay empty, but fill them with your life and keep us faithful to the end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Panchangam remembers Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos (2019) with the readings for a bishop's memory; it is also the First Friday, and the Latin Church keeps the solemnity of the Sacred Heart.
Hebrews: remember your leaders and imitate their faith; Jesus suffered outside the city gate; we have an altar; offer the sacrifice of praise and share what you have.
The faithful and wise servant feeds the household at the proper time and is found at work when the master comes.
2027-06-04.action: Make a First Friday act of love today: confession, Communion, or a visit to the Blessed Sacrament, and one gift to someone in need.
2027-06-04.question: Am I a faithful steward of what the Lord has put in my charge, or do I tell myself that the Master is delayed?

family.explain: Today we remember a bishop, Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, who went to heaven in 2019. A bishop is a shepherd for God's people. Jesus is the Good Shepherd: he loves his sheep so much that he gave his life for them. On the Cross a soldier opened Jesus' side and blood and water came out. Many Christians remember that open Heart on the First Friday of the month. It tells us how much Jesus loves each one of us.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and priests, and for Mar Timotheos, that he may rest with the Good Shepherd.
family.ask: Ask: “Who are the shepherds who have taken care of my faith, and how can I thank them?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Thiruvalla, an old sacristan kept a small notebook in the drawer beside the vestments. Over forty years he had written in it the names of the bishops who had come to the parish for confirmations, ordinations and feasts, with the date and one sentence about each visit. One line said only: he stayed after the Qurbono to bless every sick person in the parish, house by house, in the rain. When a young priest asked him why he wrote such things down, the old man said: the Letter to the Hebrews says remember your leaders; I am an old man and I forget, so I write. Then he added: I write down the good they did so that I can copy it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, good shepherd, gentle and humble of heart, we gather at your pierced side on this First Friday. Teach us to love as you love. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Which shepherd's faith do I most want to imitate?
Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood (Hebrews 13:12). What does the pierced Heart of Jesus say to me today?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What work has the Lord put in my hands?
pm.resp: Heart of Jesus, make our hearts like yours.
interc: For the soul of Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, and for all the departed bishops of our Church, that they may rest in the peace of the Good Shepherd.
For our Major Archbishop, our bishops and priests, that they may be shepherds after the heart of Christ.
For all who keep the First Friday, that their love for the Heart of Jesus may bear fruit in mercy and sharing.
For all who are hurt, lonely or tired of life, that they may find rest in the gentle and humble Heart of Jesus.
For parents, teachers and all who are stewards in God's household, that they may be found faithful at work when the Lord comes.
pm.close: Father, from the pierced side of your Son flowed blood and water, the fountain of the Church's life. Give rest to your servant Mar Timotheos, give your Church faithful shepherds, and make our hearts like the Heart of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: First Friday (ആദ്യവെള്ളി)

The custom of receiving Holy Communion on the first Friday of each month in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, often with confession beforehand, as an act of love and reparation. It spread from the seventeenth century through the devotion associated with St Margaret Mary Alacoque, and many Catholic families in Kerala, in every rite, keep it faithfully.

quick: Paul reminds Timothy of all he has seen and suffered, and tells him to continue in what he learned from childhood.
All scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching, reproof, correction and training in righteousness.
Jesus asks how the Messiah can be David's son if David calls him Lord; St Boniface, apostle of the Germans, was martyred in 754.
2027-06-05.action: Read a chapter of the Bible today with a child or a grandparent.
2027-06-05.question: Do I come to the word of God with delight, or only out of habit?

family.explain: St Paul wrote to his young friend Timothy: remember the Bible stories you learned when you were a child. Timothy's grandmother Lois and mother Eunice had taught him. Paul says that every part of the Bible is breathed by God, like God breathing life into us. Long ago a monk called Boniface loved the Bible so much that he carried it to faraway lands, and when bad men attacked him, he held the Gospel book above his head.
family.intention: We pray for all grandparents, parents and teachers who teach children about God.
family.ask: Ask: “What is my favourite Bible story, and who first told it to me?”

illus: An illustration

A woman from a parish in Kottayam district, now a doctor in a city in North India, still keeps the Bible her grandmother used. It is falling apart, the cover held together with tape, and the margins are full of dates written in pencil: the day a grandson was born, the day a son left for the Gulf, the day the old house flooded. Next to each date is a verse number. When the doctor was a child, her grandmother made her read a verse aloud every evening after the family prayer, and then asked her one question about it. She says she hated it at the time. Now, alone in a hospital flat at the end of long night shifts, she opens the book and reads the verses her grandmother chose for the hard days of her own life, and finds them still speaking.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who breathed the Scriptures, open our hearts to the word of God and give us delight in it. Amen.
share: But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it (2 Timothy 3:14). Who taught me the faith, and how can I honour them?
All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16). When did a word of Scripture correct me?
And the large crowd was listening to him with delight (Mark 12:37). What word of Jesus brings me joy?
pm.resp: Lord, your word is a lamp to my feet.
interc: For the Church, that she may love and proclaim the word of God in season and out of season.
For grandparents, parents and catechists, that they may hand on the faith to children with patience and joy.
For missionaries who carry the Gospel to new peoples, that they may have the courage of St Boniface.
For all who suffer for the faith, that the word of God may be their strength.
For the care of creation on this World Environment Day, that we may be good stewards of the earth God has given us.
pm.close: Father, you breathed your word into the Scriptures and gave us your Son, the Lord of David. Through the prayers of St Boniface, give us delight in your word and courage to hand it on. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Inspiration (ദൈവനിവേശനം)

From the Greek word in 2 Timothy 3:16, theopneustos, “God-breathed”. The Church teaches that God is the author of Sacred Scripture, and that he chose human writers who, using their own abilities, wrote everything and only what he wanted written, so that the Bible teaches without error the truth God wished to reveal for our salvation (Dei Verbum 11).
kidsaint: St Boniface and the great oak

St Boniface was a monk from England who went to teach the people of Germany about Jesus. Some of them were afraid of a huge old oak tree at Geismar that they believed was sacred to a pagan god. Boniface took an axe and cut it down, and nothing bad happened to him. The people saw that their old god had no power, and many became Christians. Boniface used the wood to build a little chapel. Many years later, when he was very old, he was killed by robbers while he waited to confirm new Christians. Lesson: do not be afraid; Jesus is stronger than anything that frightens us.

quick: Paul asks that men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument, and that women be adorned not with costly display but with good works.
The Church reads the hard verses about women within all of Scripture: man and woman are equal in dignity, created in God's image.
Jesus promises the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, who will teach and remind, and gives a peace the world cannot give.
2027-06-07.action: Make peace with one person today before you pray tonight.
2027-06-07.question: Do I come to prayer with anger I have not let go of?

family.explain: Before Jesus went back to his Father, he made two promises to his friends. First, he would send the Holy Spirit to be their helper and teacher, to remind them of everything Jesus said. Second, he gave them his peace, a peace that stays even when things are hard. St Paul also tells us that we cannot pray well when we are angry. So in our family, before night prayers, we should say sorry and make peace.
family.intention: We pray for peace in our family, and for families where there is quarrelling and anger.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone I need to make peace with before we pray tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kollam, an old couple were known for the way they ended every day. Whatever had happened, a quarrel over money, a sharp word about the children, a sulk over a burnt curry, they would not begin the family prayer until one of them had said: forgive me. Their grandchildren used to laugh at it, because sometimes the apology came in the middle of a sentence still half angry. When the old man died, his wife was asked how they had stayed so peaceful for fifty-three years. She said: we were not peaceful; we quarrelled like everyone else. But we never lifted our hands to God with the quarrel still in them.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, Advocate and teacher. Take away our anger, fill us with the peace of Christ, and remind us of all that he has said. Amen.
share: I desire, then, that in every place the men should pray, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument (1 Timothy 2:8). What anger do I need to lay down before I pray?
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything (John 14:26). What has the Holy Spirit taught me recently?
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you (John 14:27). Where do I most need the peace of Christ today?
pm.resp: Lord, give us your peace.
interc: For the Church, that the Holy Spirit may teach her everything and keep her in the truth and in peace.
For husbands and wives, that they may make peace before they pray and never let the sun set on their anger.
For women and girls in our society, that their dignity may be respected, and for all women who teach the faith in our homes and parishes.
For those whose hearts are troubled and afraid, that they may receive the peace that the world cannot give.
For students and teachers in this new school year, that the Holy Spirit may be their teacher.
pm.close: Father, through your Son you have given us peace, and through the Holy Spirit you teach and guide us. Make our hands holy and our hearts peaceful, and keep us in the truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul teaches that a person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ.
Jesus promises the Spirit of truth, who will testify to him, and he tells the disciples that they also must testify.
St Mariam Thresia (1876–1926) of Puthenchira carried that witness into the homes of the poor and the sick and founded the Congregation of the Holy Family.
2027-06-08.action: Do one hidden act of kindness for a family in need today, and thank God for the grace to do it.
2027-06-08.question: Do I quietly count my good works, as if they earned me my place before God?

family.explain: Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit, who tells the world about him. Then Jesus said: you too will tell about me. Today we remember St Mariam Thresia, who lived in Kerala about a hundred years ago. She went from house to house with her friends to help sick people, poor people and families who were fighting. She did not make speeches; her kindness told people about Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for families in our neighbourhood who are sick, poor or unhappy, that someone may bring them the love of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Which family near us needs our help, and what small thing can we do for them this week?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Thrissur district told her grandchildren how, as a small girl, she had been very ill with fever during a monsoon, when her father was away and her mother was alone with four children. Late one evening two sisters in plain habits came up the muddy path with a lantern, a little rice and some medicine. They sat with her through the night so that her mother could sleep. Years later she learned that they belonged to the congregation founded by Mariam Thresia. She said: they never told us anything about Jesus that night, but from then on I knew what he was like. Stories of this kind are told in many Kerala homes; this one is an example of the witness the Spirit gives through ordinary hands.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, Spirit of truth. Testify to Jesus in us, and through the prayers of St Mariam Thresia make our homes places of peace and our hands ready to serve. Amen.
share: A person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:16). Where do I still try to earn God's love?
He will testify on my behalf. You also are to testify (John 15:26–27). How has someone's life testified to Jesus for me?
St Mariam Thresia went into the homes of the sick and the troubled. Which home is God asking me to enter with his love?
pm.resp: Lord, make us your witnesses.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may be one table where all are welcomed by the same grace.
For the Congregation of the Holy Family and all religious who serve families, the sick and the poor.
For families broken by quarrels, debts, addiction or illness, that they may find peace and healing.
For those who have grown proud of their own goodness, that they may rediscover the joy of grace.
For our parish, that the Holy Spirit may testify to Jesus through our homes.
pm.close: Father, you justify us through faith in your Son and you send your Spirit to testify to him in us. Through the prayers of St Mariam Thresia, keep us humble before your grace and generous in serving families in need. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Domestic church (ഗാർഹികസഭ)

A name the Second Vatican Council and the Catechism give to the Christian family (Lumen Gentium 11; Catechism 1656–1657, 2204). In the home the faith is first proclaimed, prayer is learned and love is practised; the family is the Church in miniature. St Mariam Thresia devoted her life and her congregation to the holiness of families.
kidsaint: St Mariam Thresia and the lantern path

When Mariam Thresia was a young woman in Puthenchira, she and her friends went out to visit people who were very sick, even at night, carrying lamps along the village paths. They washed the sick, cooked for them, prayed with them, and stayed with the dying so that no one would die alone. Some people laughed at her, but she kept going because she saw Jesus in every sick person. Lesson: when we help someone who is weak, we are helping Jesus himself.

quick: Paul shows that when people exchange the truth about God for a lie and worship creatures, every part of life becomes disordered.
His list of sins includes gossip, envy, boasting and disobedience to parents, so that no one may judge others; all need God's grace.
At the tomb of Lazarus, Jesus tells Martha: “I am the resurrection and the life,” and she confesses him as the Messiah, the Son of God.
2027-06-09.action: Give the first ten minutes of tomorrow to God before you touch your phone.
2027-06-09.question: What created thing have I quietly put in the place of God?

family.explain: Martha and Mary were very sad because their brother Lazarus had died. Their neighbours came to comfort them. When Jesus came, Martha ran to meet him. She said: if you had been here, my brother would not have died. Jesus told her: I am the resurrection and the life. That means that Jesus is stronger than death, and those who love him will live with him for ever.
family.intention: We pray for the members of our family who have died, and for families who are sad because someone has died.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we miss who has gone to God? Let us say a prayer for that person now.”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Pathanamthitta a young father died in a road accident during the monsoon, leaving his wife and two small children. At the funeral the house was full; neighbours of every faith had come, as they do in Kerala, and sat on the verandah in the rain. When the priest read the Gospel of Lazarus, the young widow, who had not spoken all day, said Martha's words aloud after him: Yes, Lord, I believe. Months later she told the parish women's group that she still did not understand why it had happened, but that those words had held her up like a hand under her arm. She said: I could not say that everything was all right. I could only say, even now, I believe.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, turn our hearts back from every idol to the living God, and give us faith to say with Martha: even now. Amen.
share: They exchanged the truth about God for a lie (Romans 1:25). What lies about God or about myself have I believed?
Gossips, slanderers, boastful, rebellious toward parents (Romans 1:29–30). Which of these words touches my own life?
I am the resurrection and the life. Do you believe this? (John 11:25–26). What would change in me if I truly believed it?
pm.resp: Lord, I believe; raise us to life.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the truth about God with courage and receive every sinner with mercy.
For all who are caught in addictions and disorders of body or mind, that they may find healing and new life.
For those who gossip, envy and judge, ourselves first, that we may be given clean hearts.
For families who mourn, especially those who have lost someone suddenly, that they may be comforted by neighbours and by hope.
For our departed, that they may rise with Christ.
pm.close: Father, Creator of all, we have often served created things instead of you. Forgive us, turn us back to you, and through your Son, the resurrection and the life, raise us and our departed to the life that never ends. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul sends back to Philippi Epaphroditus, his brother, co-worker and fellow soldier, who nearly died in the service of Christ.
Paul asks the church to welcome him with joy and to honour such people.
Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all the truth, taking what is his and declaring it to them.
2027-06-10.action: Thank one person today whose hidden work makes your life easier.
2027-06-10.question: Which truth of faith is the Spirit patiently teaching me now, that I could not bear before?

family.explain: St Paul had a helper called Epaphroditus. He worked so hard for Jesus that he became very sick and nearly died. But God made him well again. Paul told the church: welcome him with joy and honour people like him. In every family and parish there are people who work hard and quietly for others. This week schools open again; teachers, drivers and cooks will work hard for children all year.
family.intention: We pray for teachers and all who serve children in schools, and for nurses and carers who look after the sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Who works quietly for our family, and how can we say thank you to that person this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kollam district, the parish council once decided to honour its oldest catechism teacher on the day she retired. When they counted the years, they found that she had taught on Sunday mornings for forty-one years, and that three of the priests now serving in the eparchy had been in her class. She was embarrassed by the fuss and said she had done nothing special. One of the priests stood up and said: Teacher, when I was nine and my father was in the Gulf and my mother was ill, you were the one who noticed that I had not eaten breakfast.
