You gave me your own lunch. I have forgotten most of the catechism you taught me that year, but I have never forgotten that. Every parish has people like her.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit of truth, guide us into all the truth, and teach us to honour all who labour among us for the work of Christ. Amen.
share: My brother and co-worker and fellow soldier (Philippians 2:25). Who has been a co-worker in Christ to me?
Welcome him then in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people (Philippians 2:29). Whom have I failed to honour?
I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now (John 16:12). What is the Spirit teaching me slowly?
pm.resp: Spirit of truth, guide us.
interc: For the Church, that the Holy Spirit may keep guiding her into all the truth, in fidelity to the apostles.
For catechists, sacristans, choir members and all hidden workers in our parishes.
For teachers, students and school staff at the start of the new school year, and for safety on the roads in the monsoon.
For nurses, doctors and carers, especially those from our parishes who serve far from home.
For the sick, that God may have mercy on them as he had mercy on Epaphroditus.
pm.close: Father, you raise up co-workers for the Gospel in every generation, and you send your Spirit to lead your Church into all the truth. Bless all who serve in hidden ways, heal those who are sick, and keep us faithful learners of your truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: On 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI erected the Syro-Malankara Catholic hierarchy, with the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla, after the reunion of 1930.
Paul teaches that, justified by faith and reconciled through the Son, we have peace with God, and God's love is poured into our hearts through the Spirit.
Jesus promises not to leave us orphaned: the Father and the Son make their home with those who love him; the Panchangam also remembers the apostles Bartholomew and Barnabas.
2027-06-11.action: Pray today for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our bishops, and encourage one person who needs it.
2027-06-11.question: Do I love my Church as a home given by God, and do I help to make it one for others?

family.explain: Today is a birthday for our Church. In 1932 the Pope gave our Malankara Catholic Church its own bishops and its own dioceses, so that our people would have a home in the big family of the Catholic Church. Jesus says that he and the Father come to live in the hearts of those who love him. We also remember two apostles: Bartholomew, whom Jesus praised as a man without lies, and Barnabas, whose name means son of encouragement.
family.intention: We pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and our priests, and for the unity of all Christians in Kerala and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family be a Barnabas this week and encourage someone?”

illus: An illustration

An old man in a parish near Thiruvalla used to tell his grandchildren how his own grandfather had joined the Catholic communion in the early 1930s. The family had to leave the church where they had been baptised and married, and for some years they worshipped in a thatched shed with a mud floor. When the rain came through the roof during the Qurbono, the men held umbrellas over the altar. The old man would say: we had nothing, but my grandfather used to tell us that when we heard the bishop was coming to us as our own shepherd, it was as if we had been given a house. Then he would add, more quietly: and we must never speak unkindly of the family we came from. They are still our brothers.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you do not leave us orphaned. Pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, make our Church a home where you dwell, and make us encouragers like Barnabas. Amen.
share: Since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). Where do I need God's peace today?
I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you (John 14:18). When has the Church been a home to me?
Barnabas (which means “son of encouragement”) (Acts 4:36). Whom can I encourage this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make your home with us.
interc: For the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church on the anniversary of her hierarchy: for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops, priests, religious and faithful.
For the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla, and for all our eparchies and missions in India and abroad.
For the unity of all Christians, especially for our brothers and sisters of the Malankara Orthodox and Jacobite Churches, with whom we share one heritage.
For all who are discouraged, newly converted or doubted by others, that they may meet a Barnabas.
For the Church in Armenia, Cyprus and the Middle East, lands of the apostles Bartholomew and Barnabas.
pm.close: Father, you reconciled us to yourself through the death of your Son and you pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. On this day of our Church, keep us in the unity of the one Catholic communion, make us one with all who love your Son, and let us be a home where you are glad to dwell. Through the prayers of Mar Barthulmai and Mar Barnabas, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Hierarchy, archeparchy, eparchy (ഹയരാർക്കി, അതിരൂപത, രൂപത)

The hierarchy of a Church is its ordered structure of bishops in their sees, in communion with the Bishop of Rome. In the Eastern Catholic Churches a diocese is called an eparchy and its bishop an eparch; an archeparchy is the see of a metropolitan archbishop. On 11 June 1932 the Syro-Malankara hierarchy began with one archeparchy (Thiruvananthapuram) and one eparchy (Tiruvalla).
kidsaint: Barnabas, the friend who stood up

When Saul stopped persecuting Christians and became a follower of Jesus, the disciples in Jerusalem were afraid of him. They did not believe he had really changed. Only one man was brave enough to take Saul by the hand: Barnabas. He brought Saul to the apostles and told them how Jesus had spoken to him on the road. Because Barnabas stood up for him, Saul became the great St Paul. Barnabas's name means son of encouragement. Lesson: be the one who stands up for a new or lonely friend.

quick: Paul's heart's desire and prayer is that his own people, Israel, may be saved; he loves them and honours their zeal for God.
He teaches that Christ is the end of the law, so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.
Jesus heals a suffering boy whose father begged for mercy, and tells the disciples that faith the size of a mustard seed can move mountains.
2027-06-12.action: Name three people tonight whose salvation you desire, and begin praying for them daily.
2027-06-12.question: Am I trying to establish my own righteousness, even in my prayers and fasting?

family.explain: A father had a son who was very sick; the boy often fell into the fire or into the water. The father knelt before Jesus and said: Lord, have mercy on my son. Jesus healed the boy. Then Jesus told his friends that even a very little faith, as small as a mustard seed, can do great things, because God is great. Next Wednesday our Church begins the Apostles' Fast, a time of praying and fasting together.
family.intention: We pray for children who are sick, and for parents who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “What is a mountain in our family that we can bring to Jesus with faith?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kottayam had a son who began drinking heavily after he lost his job in the Gulf. For three years he would disappear for days. She did not stop him by arguing; she had tried that. Instead, every Saturday she took the bus to a nearby church, sat for an hour before the tabernacle and prayed the father's prayer from today's Gospel: Lord, have mercy on my son. In the Apostles' Fast of the third year she added a small fast of her own, giving up her afternoon tea and putting the money in a box for a de-addiction centre. Some months later her son walked into that same centre on his own. She told the counsellor: my faith was very small, smaller than a mustard seed. But I brought him to Jesus every week.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, have mercy on our sons and daughters. Give us faith the size of a mustard seed, and prepare us to pray and fast in the Apostles' Fast. Amen.
share: My heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved (Romans 10:1). Who is the person I most long to see saved?
They have a zeal for God, but it is not enlightened (Romans 10:2). Where is my zeal for God mixed with my own pride?
Lord, have mercy on my son (Matthew 17:15). Which child, young person or family do I want to bring to Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord, increase our faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may love all people with the heart of St Paul and pray for the salvation of all.
For the Jewish people, the people of the covenant, that God may bless them and that Christians and Jews may grow in respect and friendship.
For children and young people who suffer in body or mind, and for those caught in addiction, that Jesus may heal them.
For parents who are worried about their children, that their faith may not fail.
For our parish as we prepare to begin the Apostles' Fast on Wednesday, that it may be a time of humble prayer and fasting.
pm.close: Father, Christ is the end of the law and the righteousness of all who believe. Give us Paul's love for others and the father's trust in your Son, and let our faith, small as a mustard seed, bear fruit in prayer, fasting and love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Panchangam remembers Elisha the Prophet, disciple of Elijah, who asked for a double share of his spirit and worked many signs of mercy.
At Nazareth Jesus recalls that Elisha cleansed Naaman the Syrian: God's mercy reaches beyond every border; the angry crowd cannot stop him.
Paul urges the baptised not to let sin rule their bodies but to present their members to God as instruments of righteousness: a programme for the Apostles' Fast, which begins on Wednesday.
2027-06-14.action: Decide today what you will offer to God during the Apostles' Fast.
2027-06-14.question: Which of my members, eyes, tongue, hands or appetite, most needs to be given back to God?

family.explain: Long ago there was a prophet called Elisha. A soldier from another country, Naaman, had a terrible skin disease. A little servant girl from Israel told his wife about Elisha. Naaman went to the prophet, washed seven times in the river Jordan, and was healed. Jesus told this story to show that God loves people of every nation. On Wednesday our Church begins the Apostles' Fast, when we try to give our eyes, our mouths and our hands to God.
family.intention: We pray for people of every country and every religion, that they may know God's love; and we pray for a good beginning to the Apostles' Fast.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give to God during the Apostles' Fast?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a parish in Pathanamthitta district went to work in a city in the north of India. In his hostel there was a boy from another state and another religion who was very ill with jaundice, and nobody went near him because he could not speak their language. The young man had been planning to keep the Apostles' Fast by giving up meat. Instead, he spent the fast going to the boy's room every evening with rice gruel and water, sitting with him and taking him to the hospital twice. When the boy recovered, he asked why a stranger had looked after him. The young man did not know how to explain, so he said: in my Church we are fasting now, and this was my fast. Later he told his parish priest that he had learned more about the Gospel in those two weeks than in years of catechism.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us a double share of your Spirit, and make our members instruments of righteousness as we prepare for the Apostles' Fast. Amen.
share: Present your members to God as instruments of righteousness (Romans 6:13). Which part of my life do I most need to give back to God?
None of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian (Luke 4:27). Whom do I find it hard to believe God loves?
But he passed through the midst of them and went on his way (Luke 4:30). Where do I need Jesus to pass through anger or opposition in my life?
pm.resp: Lord, make us instruments of your righteousness.
interc: For the Church, that her mercy may reach beyond every border, as the mercy of Elisha reached Naaman.
For all the baptised, that sin may not rule in their bodies, and that they may live as people brought from death to life.
For those suffering from skin diseases, leprosy and every illness that isolates people, and for those who care for them.
For migrants and strangers in our towns, that they may find neighbours who care for them.
For our parish, that the Apostles' Fast beginning on Wednesday may be kept with prayer, fasting and generosity.
pm.close: Father, through your prophets you showed mercy to the stranger, and in your Son you have brought us from death to life. Give us a double share of your Spirit, make our bodies instruments of righteousness, and let the Apostles' Fast renew us in grace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Nbiya (നിബിയ)

The Syriac word for prophet (from the same root as the Hebrew nabi), used in the Panchangam's “Eliša Nbiya” for Elisha the Prophet. In the West Syriac tradition the prophets of the Old Testament are remembered in the liturgy as those who foretold Christ and prepared his way.
kidsaint: Elisha and the little servant girl

Naaman was a great army commander, but he had a terrible skin disease. In his house there was a little girl from Israel who had been taken away from her home. She could have been angry and sad, but instead she said: I wish my master would go to the prophet Elisha; he would heal him! Naaman went, washed seven times in the river Jordan as Elisha told him, and was healed. Lesson: even a child can help someone find God's love.

quick: The Panchangam remembers the founding of the first church in the name of the holy Mother of God.
Jesus tells the Samaritan woman: the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth.
St Paul: in whatever condition you were called, remain there with God.
2027-06-15.action: Visit a church today, even for two minutes, and pray before the altar.
2027-06-15.question: Is my worship only in the church, or does it continue in my home and my work?

family.explain: Jesus met a woman at a well who asked him where people should pray to God. Jesus said that God the Father looks for people who pray with the Holy Spirit and with true hearts. We build churches so that God's family can gather and pray together, and many churches are named after Mother Mary, because she was the first home of baby Jesus. But we must also pray in our own home.
family.intention: We thank God for our parish church and pray that our home may also be a place of prayer.
family.ask: Ask: “Which church were you baptised in, and who is it named after?”

illus: An illustration

An old woman in a village near Pathanamthitta walked every morning for fifty years to St Mary's church, two kilometres along the canal. When her knees finally would not carry her, she set a small picture of the Mother of God with the Child on a shelf near the kitchen door, and when she heard the church bell across the fields she stopped her work and prayed. Her grandson once asked her whether she missed the church. She said: the church is far, but its Lord is near; and the Mother always takes me to her Son. On Sundays, when the family carried her to the Qurbono in a chair, she wept with joy at the altar. The parish priest said she had understood both halves of the Gospel: the house of God and the worship in spirit and truth.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you make us true worshippers of the Father. Teach us to pray in your house and in our homes, with the holy Mother of God who kept the word in her heart. Amen.
share: The true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth (John 4:23). What helps me to pray truly, and what distracts me?
Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built (1 Kings 8:27). What does my parish church mean to me?
In whatever condition you were called, brothers and sisters, there remain with God (1 Corinthians 7:24). Where is God asking me to be faithful just now?
pm.resp: Father, make us your true worshippers.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that her churches may be houses of prayer for all peoples.
For our parish church and all churches named after the holy Mother of God, that those who pray in them may find her Son.
For those who cannot come to church because of age, illness or distance, that the Lord may visit them at home.
For students and teachers as the new school year begins, that their work may be offered to God.
For Christians of all Churches who honour the Mother of God, that she may lead us to unity in her Son.
pm.close: Lord God, Mary, the Mother of your Son, became the first dwelling of your Word, and the first church built in her name has many children in our land. Make us living temples of your Spirit, faithful in your house and faithful in our daily work, and bring us at last to your house in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Today the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) begins; it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June.
Jesus gives the Twelve authority over unclean spirits and every sickness; Matthew lists their names.
St Paul: we are servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries, and stewards must be found trustworthy.
2027-06-16.action: Choose one concrete fast for these days and one person to whom you will give what it saves.
2027-06-16.question: What has God entrusted to me, and am I a trustworthy steward of it?

family.explain: Today the Apostles' Fast begins. Jesus chose twelve friends, called them by name, and sent them to tell everyone about God's love. One of them, St Thomas, came to our own land. The apostles prayed and fasted before they went out to preach. In these days we also give up something small, pray a little more and share with the poor, so that the Good News can reach many people.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, for our bishop and for our parish priest, who carry on the work of the apostles.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can our family give up during this fast, and whom shall we help with it?”

illus: An illustration

A family in Mavelikara sat down together on the evening before the Apostles' Fast to decide how to keep it. The father suggested the usual abstinence from meat and fish. The teenage son, after some hesitation, offered to give up the online games that ate up his evenings. The youngest daughter said she would keep the coins from her snack money in a tin. Then the grandmother asked: and for whom are we fasting? They decided on two things: the money would go towards the operation of a neighbour's child, and every night they would pray for the parish priest, who had been ill. On the feast of Sts Peter and Paul they opened the tin and counted the coins together. The amount was not large, but the neighbour wept when it was given, and the priest, recovered, came to bless the house.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at the start of the Apostles' Fast we gather in your name. Give us the spirit of your apostles: prayer, self-denial and zeal for your Gospel. Amen.
share: Then Jesus summoned his twelve disciples and gave them authority (Matthew 10:1). How do I see the apostolic Church in my bishop and my parish?
Think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries (1 Corinthians 4:1). What has God entrusted to my care?
Do not pronounce judgment before the time (1 Corinthians 4:5). Whom do I judge too quickly?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful stewards.
interc: For the Holy Father, Pope Leo, successor of St Peter, and for all the bishops, successors of the apostles.
For our major archbishop, our bishops and all our priests, that they may be found trustworthy stewards of God's mysteries.
For missionaries in distant places, that the Spirit who sent Barnabas and Saul may strengthen them.
For all the Christians of Kerala who keep the Apostles' Fast in these days, that our prayer and fasting may draw us closer to one another.
For the poor who will receive the alms of this fast, that they may know the love of God.
pm.close: Lord God, your apostles fasted and prayed and were sent out by your Spirit. As we begin this fast, purify our hearts, make us trustworthy stewards of your gifts, keep us from judging others, and send us out as witnesses of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Shleeha Nombu (ശ്ലീഹാ നോമ്പ്)

The Apostles' Fast. Shleeha is the Syriac word for apostle (one who is sent) and nombu is the Malayalam word for a fast. Kept by the Churches of the Syriac tradition after Pentecost, it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June. In 2027 the Panchangam marks its beginning on 16 June.

quick: Jesus: the one who hears my words and acts on them is like a man who built his house on rock.
St Paul: continue to live in Christ, rooted and built up in him; in him the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily.
God erased the record that stood against us and nailed it to the cross.
2027-06-17.action: Do one thing today that Jesus asks of you and that you have been putting off.
2027-06-17.question: Which word of Jesus do I hear often but have never really put into practice?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about two men who built houses. One dug deep and built on a rock; the other built on loose ground. When the big rain and the flood came, the house on the rock stood strong, but the other one fell down. Jesus says that listening to him and doing what he says is like building on rock. During the monsoon we see how strong water is; we need a strong foundation, and Jesus is our rock.
family.intention: We pray for families whose homes are in danger from floods and heavy rain this monsoon.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asks us to do that our family will really do this week?”

illus: An illustration

After the great floods of 2018, an engineer from Chengannur who helped to inspect damaged houses told a parish meeting what he had seen. Along one road, two houses stood side by side, built in the same year, painted the same colour. One had cracked from top to bottom; the other had only a line of mud on its walls. Nobody could see the difference from the road. The difference was underground: the first owner had saved money on the foundation, the second had insisted on digging down to hard laterite. The engineer said that he had read the parable of the two builders all his life, but he only understood it when he stood between those two houses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the rock on which we build. Open our ears to your word and our hands to do it, and keep us firm in every flood. Amen.
share: Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you? (Luke 6:46). Where do I say yes to Jesus with my lips and no with my life?
Rooted and built up in him and established in the faith (Colossians 2:7). What helps my roots go deeper?
He set this aside, nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:14). Is there a sin I still carry although Christ has forgiven it?
pm.resp: Lord, be the rock of our lives.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be built on the rock of Christ and of the apostolic faith.
For all who are keeping the Apostles' Fast, that their fasting may root them more deeply in Christ.
For families threatened by floods and landslides in this monsoon, and for those who have lost their homes.
For the newly baptised, that they may grow rooted and built up in Christ.
For those who hear the word of God but find it hard to live it, that grace may reach their hearts.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you have given us the fullness of life and cancelled the record of our debt. Make us doers of his word and not hearers only, rooted in him, built up in him and abounding in thanksgiving, so that no flood may sweep us away. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Today we remember Mar Aprem Malpan, St Ephrem the Syrian, deacon, poet and Doctor of the Church, called the Harp of the Spirit.
Hebrews: the law has only a shadow of the good things to come; the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins.
Jesus: I do not call you servants any longer, but friends; love one another as I have loved you.
2027-06-18.action: Sing or read slowly one hymn of our liturgy today, and thank God for what it teaches.
2027-06-18.question: Do I know Jesus as a friend, or only as a master to be obeyed?

family.explain: Jesus tells his disciples that they are not his servants but his friends, and that the greatest love is to give your life for your friends. Today we remember Mar Aprem, a holy deacon who lived long ago in Syria. He loved Jesus so much that he wrote many beautiful songs about him, and he taught people to sing them. When there was a famine, he helped the hungry. He was a true friend of Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for all who teach the faith, especially through music and song.
family.ask: Ask: “What is your favourite hymn, and what does it tell us about Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Thiruvalla, an old choir master used to begin every practice with the same words: we are not here to perform, we are here to pray twice. One evening a teenage girl asked him why the old Syriac melodies mattered when the young people preferred new songs. He answered with a story. Sixteen centuries ago, he said, a deacon named Ephrem noticed that heretics were teaching wrong ideas about Christ through catchy tunes. Instead of only arguing, he wrote better songs, true songs, and taught them to choirs of women, who sang them in the streets and the churches until the whole city knew the true faith by heart. Then the choir master said: every time you sing the hymns of our Church, you are carrying the faith home in a melody. The girl stayed in the choir, and years later she was teaching the hymns to children herself.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have called us your friends. With Mar Aprem, the Harp of the Spirit, we praise you; teach us to see you in your word and to love one another as you have loved us. Amen.
share: The law has only a shadow of the good things to come (Hebrews 10:1). Where in the Old Testament have I discovered Christ?
I have called you friends (John 15:15). What does friendship with Jesus mean in my daily life?
I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). What fruit is Jesus asking me to bear now?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your friendship.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may proclaim the one sacrifice of Christ and the friendship he offers to all.
For our Syriac Churches, Catholic and Orthodox, who love Mar Aprem, that his prayer may draw us to unity.
For deacons, catechists, choir members and all who teach the faith through word and song.
For the hungry and for those who suffer from famine and poverty, that they may find friends who help them.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that their self-denial may bear fruit in love.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave your Church Mar Aprem Malpan, deacon and teacher, who sang your mysteries with the harp of the Spirit. Through his prayers, let us see your Son in every page of Scripture, love one another as he loved us, and bear fruit that will last. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Malpan (മല്പാൻ)

From the Syriac malpana, teacher. In the Syriac tradition it is the title of a learned teacher of the Scriptures and the faith; in Kerala it was given to the masters who taught Syriac and theology to future priests. Mar Aprem is called Malpan because his hymns and commentaries taught the whole Church.
kidsaint: Mar Aprem, the harp of the Holy Spirit

Long ago in Syria there lived a deacon named Ephrem, Aprem in our language. Some people were teaching wrong things about Jesus with songs that were easy to remember. Ephrem did not just argue with them. He wrote new songs, full of true and beautiful words about Jesus and Mother Mary, and taught them to choirs of women and girls. Soon the whole town was singing the true faith! People called him the harp of the Holy Spirit. Lesson: you can share your love for Jesus by singing.

quick: Hebrews: coming into the world, Christ said, “See, God, I have come to do your will”; we are sanctified by the offering of his body once for all.
Jesus: do not resist an evildoer; turn the other cheek, go the second mile, love your enemies.
Today we remember Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, St Jude, one of the Twelve, invoked as a helper in desperate causes.
2027-06-19.action: Do one kind thing today for someone who has been unkind to you.
2027-06-19.question: Whom do I still need to forgive, and will I pray for that person today?

family.explain: Jesus teaches us something very hard: not to hit back when someone hurts us, but to be kind instead, and even to pray for people who are unkind to us. This is what Jesus did on the Cross. Today we also remember St Jude, one of Jesus' twelve apostles. Many people pray to him when they have big problems, because he reminds us that nothing is impossible for God.
family.intention: We pray for people who are angry with each other, in families, in our neighbourhood and in the world, that they may make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone who hurt us whom we can forgive and pray for tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A bus conductor on the Kottayam route was insulted every day for a month by the same passenger, a young man who refused to pay the full fare and mocked him in front of everyone. The conductor's friends told him to throw the boy off the bus. One morning the young man boarded pale and shaking; his mother had been taken to the medical college hospital in the night. The conductor saw that he had no money at all. Without a word he punched a ticket, put it in his hand, and at the hospital stop he walked him to the gate. A week later the young man came back to the bus, paid his fare, and said quietly: you went the second mile for me. The conductor only smiled. He told his family that evening that he had been praying for the boy every night of the Apostles' Fast.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came to do the Father's will and loved your enemies to the end. Give us hearts that do not pay back evil with evil, and with St Jude, teach us to trust you in every need. Amen.
share: See, God, I have come to do your will (Hebrews 10:7). Where is the Father's will hardest for me to accept just now?
If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Where can I go the second mile this week?
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Whom do I find it hardest to pray for?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love as you love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a sign of reconciliation in a world divided by revenge.
For all who are persecuted for their faith, and for those who persecute them.
For families and neighbours divided by quarrels, that someone may take the first step to peace.
For all who bring desperate needs to the prayers of St Jude, that they may find help and hope.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that they may fast also from anger and revenge.
pm.close: Father, your Son came into the world to do your will and offered his body for us once for all. Make us one with his obedience and his love, that we may overcome evil with good. Through the prayers of the apostle Mar Yuda Thaddai, help us in every need and make your home in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

kidsaint: St Jude, the apostle with a question

St Jude was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. At the Last Supper he asked Jesus a question: Lord, why will you show yourself to us and not to the whole world? Jesus gave him a beautiful answer: if you love me and keep my word, my Father and I will come and live in your heart. Today many people pray to St Jude when they have very big problems, because he reminds us that God is always near. Lesson: you can ask Jesus any question and bring him any problem.

quick: The disciples argued about who was the greatest; Jesus said: whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.
He placed a child among them: whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.
St Paul: present your members as slaves to righteousness; the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life. Today we remember St Aloysius Gonzaga.
2027-06-21.action: Do one hidden service today for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-06-21.question: In what part of my life do I still want to be the greatest?

family.explain: On the road the disciples argued about who was the most important. Jesus told them that the most important person is the one who serves everyone. Then he took a little child in his arms and said that when we welcome a child, we welcome Jesus himself. Today we remember St Aloysius, a rich boy who could have become a prince, but chose to serve God and to care for sick people. He is the patron of students.
family.intention: We pray for all students and teachers beginning the new school year, and for children who are neglected or alone.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our school, class or street is often left out, and how can we welcome that person this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a higher secondary school in Kollam, the class leader was chosen each June by votes, and every year there was a fierce competition. One year the boy who won surprised the class: on the first day he stayed back after school to sweep the classroom with the cleaning staff, and he did it every Friday for the rest of the year. When his friends teased him, he said that his grandfather had given him a holy card of St Aloysius on the first day of school, with the words: the leader is the one who serves. By December, nobody was arguing about who was greatest in that class; the arguments had moved on to who would help him sweep.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you made yourself the servant of all. Take from us the desire to be greatest, and with St Aloysius teach us to serve you in the least of our brothers and sisters. Amen.
share: What were you arguing about on the way? (Mark 9:33). What do I argue about that I would not want Jesus to hear?
You are slaves of the one whom you obey (Romans 6:16). What or whom am I really serving with my time and energy?
Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me (Mark 9:37). Whom am I being asked to welcome?
pm.resp: Lord, make us servants of all.
interc: For the Church and her pastors, that they may lead by serving, after the example of Christ.
For students and teachers in this new academic year, that St Aloysius may guide them in purity of heart and generosity.
For young people who are searching for their path in life, that they may hear the call of Christ.
For the sick, especially those with contagious diseases, and for all who nurse them at risk to themselves.
For children who are neglected, abused or alone, that they may be welcomed as Christ himself.
pm.close: Father, your Son placed a child in the midst of his disciples and taught them that the first must be the servant of all. Through the prayers of St Aloysius Gonzaga, give us humble and pure hearts, make us servants of righteousness, and lead us to the gift of eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

kidsaint: St Aloysius carries a sick man

Aloysius was born into a very rich family in Italy. He could have become a prince, but he loved Jesus more than money or power, so he joined the Jesuits. When a terrible sickness spread in Rome, many people were afraid to go near the sick. Aloysius went to the streets, lifted a sick man onto his shoulders and carried him to the hospital. He caught the sickness himself and died when he was only twenty-three. Lesson: the greatest person is the one who serves.

quick: St Paul compares giving to sowing: the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
Each one should give gladly, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
Jesus says: store up treasures in heaven, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
2027-06-22.action: Give away today, gladly and quietly, what you would have spent on something you do not need.
2027-06-22.question: Where is my treasure, and therefore where is my heart?

family.explain: A farmer who wants a big harvest does not plant only a few seeds. St Paul says giving is like planting: when we share what we have, it is not lost, it grows. God loves people who give with a smile, not with a grumble. Jesus says that what we keep only for ourselves can be spoiled or stolen, but what we give with love is kept safe in heaven.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough food this monsoon, and for the grace to share gladly.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing I can share this week with a smile?”

illus: An illustration

In many old Kerala Christian homes there was a small pot in the kitchen for the pidiyari, the handful of rice. Each time the rice for the family meal was measured out, the mother would take one handful and put it into that pot. At the end of the week the pot went to the church, to the poor, or to a neighbour whose kitchen was empty. A grandmother in Kuttanad, asked by her grandson why she still did it when everyone now gave money in envelopes, said: a handful is nothing to the pot, but it is everything to the heart, because it means that every single meal in this house remembers someone else. Then she added, laughing, that in sixty years of taking out the handful, the family rice had never once run short.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, giver of every good gift, make our hearts glad and generous. In this fast of the Apostles teach us to sow bountifully and to store up treasure in heaven. Amen.
share: The one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). When have I seen a small gift grow into something great?
God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). Do I give gladly, or only because I must?
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Matthew 6:21). What do I worry about losing most?
pm.resp: Lord, make us cheerful givers.
interc: For the Church in this Apostles' Fast, that her prayer, fasting and almsgiving may please the Lord.
For the poor, the jobless and families struggling through the monsoon months, that they may find generous neighbours.
For farmers sowing their fields in these rains, that their labour may be blessed with a good harvest.
For those who are anxious about money, that they may trust in the God who supplies seed to the sower.
For our parish, that we may share abundantly in every good work.
pm.close: Father, you give seed to the sower and bread for food. Make us generous with what you have given us, glad in our giving, and delivered from the fear of want, so that our treasure and our hearts may be with you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul sends Tychicus, a dear brother and faithful minister, to encourage the hearts of the Ephesians.
Jesus finds the man born blind after he is driven out; the man says, “Lord, I believe”, and worships him.
Those who claim to see without needing the light remain in their sin.
2027-06-23.action: Encourage one person today with a visit, a call or a message of good news.
2027-06-23.question: Where do I say “I see” when I really need the Lord to open my eyes?

family.explain: A man who had been blind from birth was healed by Jesus. But some people were angry and threw him out. Jesus did not forget him; he went looking for him. When the man understood who Jesus was, he said: Lord, I believe! and he knelt down to worship. Jesus always looks for people who are left out, and he wants us to do the same.
family.intention: We pray for the blind and for everyone who feels left out, at school, at work or at home.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone left out in my class or at work whom I can go and find, as Jesus did?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in the Pathanamthitta area once held an eye camp in its hall, with treatment at no cost, and among the patients was an old man who had lived for some years in the fog of cataracts. A few days after his operation, when the bandages came off, his granddaughter was standing in front of him. He looked at her for a long time and then began to cry, because he had not seen her face since she was a baby. The next Sunday he came to the Holy Qurbono early, sat in the front row and did not take his eyes off the altar. When the priest asked him why, he said: for years I came here and heard everything and saw nothing; now I want to see everything I heard.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, open the eyes of our hearts. Find us when we are lost, and teach us to say with all our heart: Lord, I believe. Amen.
share: He is a dear brother and a faithful minister in the Lord (Ephesians 6:21). Who has been a Tychicus for me, encouraging my heart?
Jesus heard that they had driven him out, and when he found him (John 9:35). When did Jesus come looking for me?
Now that you say, ‘We see,’ your sin remains (John 9:41). Where am I too sure of myself?
pm.resp: Lord, I believe; open my eyes.
interc: For all who carry the word of God quietly, catechists, teachers and messengers of the gospel, that they may be faithful like Tychicus.
For those who have been driven out or rejected, that Jesus may find them and they may find a welcome among us.
For the blind and those losing their sight, and for doctors who treat the eyes, that the Lord may bless them.
For catechumens and those preparing for Baptism, that they may receive the light of Christ.
For our parish in this Apostles' Fast, that we may grow in humility and in an undying love for our Lord Jesus Christ.
pm.close: Father, your Son came into the world as its light. Open our eyes to see him, our lips to confess him and our knees to worship him, and keep us humble enough to know our need of him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Elizabeth gives birth to a son, and her neighbours and relatives rejoice at the mercy the Lord has shown her.
Against family custom the child is named John, as the angel had said; Zechariah writes “His name is John”, and his tongue is loosened to praise God.
The Epistle calls us to pursue peace and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord; the Panchangam also remembers Cheppattu Philipose Ramban.
2027-06-24.action: Pray the Benedictus, the canticle of Zechariah (Luke 1:68–79), slowly today.
2027-06-24.question: What does God want me to become, and am I letting him write my name?

family.explain: Zechariah and Elizabeth were old and had no children, and God gave them a baby. Everyone wanted to call him Zechariah, like his father. But God had already chosen his name: John, which means God is kind. Zechariah could not speak, so he wrote on a tablet: His name is John! At once he could speak again, and the first thing he did was to praise God. John grew up to be the one who showed people Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for all the children of our family and our parish as the new school year begins, that God's hand may be with them.
family.ask: Ask: “Why was your name chosen? Let us thank God for the name each of us received at Baptism.”

illus: An illustration

In a family near Kottayam the first grandson was born, and the grandfather, a strong-willed man, announced at once that the boy would carry his name, as the custom was. The young parents had prayed through a difficult pregnancy and had promised to name the child after the saint whose intercession they had asked. For some days the house was tense. On the day of the baptism, the grandfather stood beside the font and heard the priest ask, What name do you give this child? The father answered with the saint's name. Afterwards, at lunch, the old man stood up, raised his glass of water, and said: I wanted the child to carry my name; but I have been thinking of Zechariah, who had to write a name he had not chosen. Let the boy carry the name God gave him, and let him carry my blessing too. The family says it was the best speech he ever made.

pm.open: Lord God, you gave John to Zechariah and Elizabeth as a sign of your great mercy. Open our lips to praise you, and let your hand be on us and on our children. Amen.
share: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her (Luke 1:58). When have I rejoiced with someone at the mercy God showed them?
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, His name is John (Luke 1:63). Where is God asking me to obey him rather than custom or opinion?
What then will this child become? (Luke 1:66). What do I hope for the children I know, and do I pray for them?
pm.resp: Lord, let your hand be with us.
interc: For the Church, that like John the Baptist she may always point to Christ, the Lamb of God.
For children and young people beginning the new school year, that the hand of the Lord may be with them.
For couples waiting for a child, that they may know the mercy God showed to Zechariah and Elizabeth.
For the monks, priests and teachers who spoke the word of God to us, especially Cheppattu Philipose Ramban whose memory we keep, that the Lord may reward them.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that they may pursue peace and holiness and never sell their birthright for a single meal.
pm.close: Lord God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way for your Son. Give your Church the joy of his birth, the courage of his witness and the humility of his heart, so that Christ may increase in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Mamdana (മാംദാനാ)
The Syriac word for the Baptizer, from the verb meaning to baptize. In the Syro-Malankara and other Syriac traditions John the Baptist is called Yohannan Mamdana, John the Baptizer.
kidsaint: Zechariah's writing tablet

When the baby was born, everyone wanted to call him Zechariah, like his father. His father could not speak, because he had doubted the angel's message. So he asked for a writing tablet and wrote in big letters: His name is John. At that very moment his mouth was opened, and he began to praise God! Lesson: when we obey God, even in small things, our hearts and our mouths are opened to praise him.

quick: By faith Abraham was ready to offer Isaac, trusting that God could even raise the dead.
By faith Isaac, Jacob and Joseph blessed the generations to come, though they did not see the promise fulfilled.
Jesus says his teaching comes from the Father; whoever does God's will shall know it. Do not judge by appearances.
2027-06-25.action: Bless a child or a younger person today with the sign of the cross, and pray for their future.
2027-06-25.question: Do I judge people by appearances, or do I try to see them as God sees them?

family.explain: Long ago, when Isaac and Jacob were very old, they blessed their children and grandchildren and asked God to take care of them. In our family too, grandparents and parents bless children with the sign of the cross. Jesus also tells us not to judge people by how they look, but to look at their hearts, as God does.
family.intention: We pray for all the grandparents and parents in our family, and for the children who receive their blessing.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or at work whom I have judged by how they look? How can I get to know them better?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Idukki has blessed her children every morning since they were small: before they leave the house, she makes the sign of the cross on their foreheads with her thumb and whispers a short prayer. Her eldest son is now a policeman and wears a uniform and a cap, and she still does it at the door, standing on tiptoe. Once a colleague who had come to pick him up laughed and asked whether he still needed his mother's permission to go to work. The son answered quietly: it is not permission, it is a blessing, and in my job I have learned to want every blessing I can get. Some weeks later the same colleague asked her, a little shyly, whether she would bless him too.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us the faith of Abraham and the faith of our fathers and mothers. Teach us to bless those who come after us, and to judge with right judgment. Amen.
share: By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac (Hebrews 11:17). What test has God allowed in my life, and how have I answered?
By faith Isaac invoked blessings for the future on Jacob and Esau (Hebrews 11:20). Who blessed me, and whom do I bless?
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment (John 7:24). Whom have I judged unfairly?
pm.resp: Lord, increase our faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may hand on the faith of the Apostles faithfully to the next generation.
For grandparents and parents, that they may bless their children and teach them by their example.
For children and students at the start of the school year, that they may grow in wisdom and in grace.
For all who are judged unfairly because of their appearance, their caste, their poverty or their past, that they may find justice and respect.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that their hearts may be purified and their judgements made right.
pm.close: Father, you tested the faith of Abraham and gave him back his son. Strengthen our faith in times of trial, make us a blessing to those who come after us, and teach us to see others with your eyes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul thanks the Philippians, the one church that kept on sharing with him in giving and receiving.
Their gift is a fragrant offering pleasing to God, and God will fully satisfy every need of theirs.
Jesus warns against the father of lies: whoever is from God hears the words of God.
2027-06-26.action: Speak only what is true and kind today, and forward no message you have not checked.
2027-06-26.question: Do I share in the work of the gospel, and do my words come from the truth?

family.explain: The Christians of Philippi did not have much, but they sent gifts to St Paul so that he could keep telling people about Jesus. Paul said their gift was like sweet-smelling incense rising to God. Tomorrow our Church asks us to help the seminary, where young men are trained to become priests. Jesus also says that God's children listen to God's word and speak the truth.
family.intention: We pray for the seminarians of our Church, that they may become holy priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family give tomorrow for the seminary, and what can we do to always speak the truth?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish family group on the phone, an uncle forwarded a message one evening claiming that a well-known neighbour had been arrested for cheating. Within an hour it had been forwarded to three other groups. His niece, a college student, did not reply in the group. She called the neighbour's daughter, a friend of hers, and learned that the story was completely false; the man had been in hospital with his wife. She then wrote to her uncle privately. The next morning, before anyone else could say anything, the uncle wrote in every group where he had sent the message: I passed on a lie about a good man. I am sorry. Please delete it. At the Sunday Qurbono he went to the neighbour and apologised in person. The neighbour said it was the first time in his life that a rumour about him had been taken back.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you speak the truth and you came from the Father. Make us hearers of your word, people of truth, and generous partners in your gospel. Amen.
share: No church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving, except you alone (Philippians 4:15). Do I share in the work of the gospel by my giving?
A fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God (Philippians 4:18). What offering can I make this week?
Whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47). How well do I listen to the word of God?
pm.resp: Lord, make us children of the truth.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the truth of Christ with courage and with love.
For our Major Seminary, its formators and seminarians, that they may grow in holiness and be ready to be sent like the Apostles.
For all who give generously to the work of the gospel, that the Lord may supply every need of theirs.
For those who have been hurt by lies and rumours, that their good name may be restored.
For ourselves, that in this Apostles' Fast we may keep the fast of the tongue and speak only what is true.
pm.close: Father, from you comes every good gift. Accept our offerings as a fragrant sacrifice, keep us in your truth, and supply all our needs according to your riches in glory in Christ Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul tells Timothy to avoid wrangling over words and to be a worker who rightly explains the word of truth.
Mar Irenaeus, who learned the faith from St Polycarp, defended the faith of the Apostles handed down in the Church and worked for peace.
Jesus chose the Apostles and appointed them to bear fruit that will last, and commanded them to love one another.
2027-06-28.action: Thank God today, by name, for the people who handed on the faith to you.
2027-06-28.question: Do I help others to understand the faith, or do I only argue about it?

family.explain: Jesus chose his Apostles and sent them to tell everyone about God's love. They taught others, and those taught others again, like a long chain of hands passing on a lamp. St Irenaeus, whom we remember today, learned about Jesus from an old bishop, St Polycarp, who had known the Apostle John. Our parents and grandparents are part of that chain too, and now we are.
family.intention: We pray for our bishop Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day, and for all who teach the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught me to pray? Let us thank God for that person tonight.”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a small parish near Mavelikkara retired after teaching the Sunday class for forty years. At her farewell, the parish priest asked those in the church who had learned their prayers from her to stand up. Grandfathers stood, and their sons, and their grandchildren; the young assistant priest stood, and so did two religious sisters who were visiting their families. Almost the whole church was on its feet. The old teacher could not speak. When she finally took the microphone, she said only this: I learned the Our Father from my grandmother, who learned it from hers. I did not teach you anything of my own. I only passed it on as straight as I could.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you chose us and sent us to bear fruit that will last. Through the prayers of Mar Irenaeus, keep us in the faith of the Apostles, in peace and in love. Amen.
share: Avoid wrangling over words, which does no good (2 Timothy 2:14). Where do I quarrel when I should build up?
A worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth (2 Timothy 2:15). How well do I know and explain my faith?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it change my life to know that Christ chose me?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in the faith of your Apostles.
interc: For the Church, that she may guard the faith received from the Apostles with one heart and one voice.
For Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day, and for all our bishops, that they may be teachers of the truth and servants of unity.
For catechists, teachers and parents who hand on the faith, that they may explain the word of truth rightly.
For an end to quarrels and divisions among Christians, that all may be one.
For all who have kept the Apostles' Fast, that they may celebrate the feast of Sts Peter and Paul with renewed faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave Mar Irenaeus the grace to guard the faith of the Apostles and to work for peace. Keep your Church faithful to the teaching she has received, united in charity, and fruitful in every good work. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Name day (നാമഹേതുക തിരുനാൾ)

The feast of the saint whose name a person bears. In the Syro-Malankara Church, as in other Syriac Churches, a bishop receives a new name at his episcopal ordination, usually the name of a saint or Father of the Church preceded by the title Mar; the feast of that saint is kept as his name day, and the faithful pray for him on that day.
kidsaint: Young Irenaeus remembers

When Irenaeus was a boy, he loved to sit and listen to an old bishop named Polycarp. Polycarp told stories about the Apostle John, who had been Jesus' friend. Many years later, when Irenaeus was himself an old bishop, he wrote that he could still remember the very place where Polycarp sat and the way he spoke. Lesson: listen carefully to the people who tell you about Jesus. One day you will pass it on too.

quick: Jesus went up the mountain, called those whom he wanted, and appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out to proclaim the message.
The Twelve were very different men, from Simon Peter to Thomas, who brought the gospel to India, made one around Christ.
Paul describes the apostolic life: now is the acceptable time; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
2027-06-30.action: Spend fifteen minutes with Jesus in prayer today, and then do one thing to share him with someone.
2027-06-30.question: Am I spending enough time with Jesus to be sent by him?

family.explain: Jesus chose twelve friends to be his Apostles. First he wanted them to be with him, to listen to him and to pray with him. Then he sent them out to tell everyone about God's love. They were very different: fishermen, a tax collector, quiet men and loud men. One of them, St Thomas, came all the way to India. Jesus calls us too: to be with him and to share his love.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and our bishops, the successors of the Apostles, and for missionaries everywhere.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we name all twelve Apostles together? Which one would you like to know more about?”

illus: An illustration

A religious sister from a village near Adoor left home at nineteen with one small suitcase to work among the poor in a mission in central India. For thirty years she taught in a village school and ran a dispensary, often with no electricity and little money. When she came home on leave, a niece asked her, a little sadly, whether she did not regret owning nothing at all. The sister laughed and began to count on her fingers the families who welcomed her into their homes, the children who had become teachers and nurses, the old people who called her their daughter. Then she said: I have no house, but I have a hundred homes. I came with one suitcase and I have more than I can carry. Her niece later found the same idea in St Paul: as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the Twelve to be with you and sent them out to proclaim the good news. Call us to be with you, and send us out as your witnesses, through the prayers of your holy Apostles. Amen.
share: He called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him (Mark 3:13). How did Jesus call me, and how did I come?
to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message (Mark 3:14). Do I spend time with him before I try to work for him?
as having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). What do I possess because I have Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out as your witnesses.
interc: For Pope Leo XIV, the successor of Peter, and for all bishops, the successors of the Apostles, that they may guard and spread the apostolic faith.
For missionaries who have left home and family to proclaim the gospel, that they may be sorrowful yet always rejoicing.
For the Syro-Malankara Church and all the Churches of St Thomas in India, that they may be faithful to the faith of the Apostle.
For Christians who suffer for their faith, as the Apostles did, that they may be strengthened.
For our parish, that we may be with Jesus in prayer and be sent by him into our daily lives.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the foundation of the Apostles. Through their prayers keep us faithful to their teaching, united in their communion, and eager to be sent as they were. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Shleeha (ശ്ലീഹാ)

The Syriac word for apostle, meaning one who is sent, from the verb to send; it corresponds to the Greek word apostolos. The plural is Shleeheh, in Malayalam ശ്ലീഹന്മാർ. Mar Thoma Shleeha is St Thomas the Apostle.
kidsaint: Twelve very different friends

Jesus chose twelve friends, and they were not all the same. Peter, Andrew, James and John were fishermen. Matthew collected taxes, and people did not like him. Simon the Cananaean was a man with strong opinions. James and John were so loud and fiery that Jesus called them Sons of Thunder! But Jesus loved them all and taught them to love one another. Thomas, one of them, came all the way to India. Lesson: in Jesus' family, everyone has a place, and we must be friends with those who are different from us.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus went to his own town and was rejected. “Prophets are not without honor, except in their hometown.” Did he give up? No. He called the Twelve and sent them out two by two. They preached repentance, cast out demons, and anointed the sick with oil. The mission of the Church began with rejection, and went on in the power of God.

In the Gospel of John Jesus says: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry… anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.” What a promise! No sinner who comes to him is turned away. And he says: “No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father.” If you are here today, the Father has drawn you.

In the book of Daniel three young men refuse to worship the golden statue. They say: our God can save us from the fire; “but if not,” we still will not worship your gods. This is mature faith. It does not say “God, if you give me this, I will believe.” It says “God, whatever happens, I belong to you.” Our Malankara Church, born in 1930 with Mar Ivanios, knows this faith: they left property and buildings, but kept communion.

St Paul says: let us do good to all, and boast only in the Cross; what matters is a new creation. This week, go two by two: visit a sick or lonely person with someone from your family. And come often to the bread of life. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent his friends out two by two, like partners, to tell people about God and to help sick people.
In the Bible, three brave young men would not bow to a golden statue, even when the king was angry. They loved God more than anything!
Jesus says: “I am the bread of life.” Who can you visit this week with your mum, dad or friend?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the day is ending, the crowd is hungry, and the disciples want to send them away. Jesus says: “You give them something to eat.” They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus takes them, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and gives them to the disciples to give to the people. All eat and are satisfied, and twelve baskets are left over.

Notice: Jesus does not drop bread from the sky. He feeds the crowd through the hands of his disciples. That is the mystery of the priesthood. At every Holy Qurbono a man takes bread, and Christ through his hands feeds his people. Today we pray for those hands: our priests, and the young men in our seminaries.

But the disciples also had to learn. In the evening Gospel they argued about who was the greatest. Jesus took a child in his arms and said: “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.” A priest, a parent, a leader is great only by serving.

God chooses surprising people. He chose Saul, the persecutor, and sent Ananias to lay hands on him. He may be choosing a boy or girl in your family. Do not say “not my son, not my daughter.” Offer your five loaves. And to all who are weary in service, Isaiah says: “Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” Amen.
kids: Children, a boy had five little loaves and two fish. He gave them to Jesus, and Jesus fed five thousand people!
Jesus gave the bread to his friends to share. Today priests share the Bread of Jesus with us at the Holy Qurbono.
Let's pray for priests and for boys who are learning to become priests. And what small thing will you give to Jesus?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus tells of a shepherd who has a hundred sheep and loses one. Ninety-nine are safe; why bother about one? But he leaves them and searches until he finds it. Then he lays it on his shoulders, joyful, and calls his friends: “Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.” That is how God looks at each of us. Not as a number, but as the one he is searching for.

St Paul says the Church is a body. “If one member suffers, all suffer together with it; if one member is honoured, all rejoice.” Our families are the first place we learn this. In a good family no one is left behind, not the sick grandparent, not the child who struggles in school, not the son or daughter who has wandered away.

In the evening Gospel Jesus asks something very hard: forgive your brother seven times in a day if he repents. The apostles cry out: “Increase our faith!” We cannot forgive like that by our own strength. We need faith that God is bigger than our hurt. And when we have done all this, Jesus says, we should say humbly: “We have done only what we ought to have done.”

Paul tells the Athenians: God “is not far from each one of us; in him we live and move and have our being.” Who is the lost sheep in your family, your street, your parish? Call them this week. Pray for them. Light the lamp for them in the evening. And let heaven rejoice. Amen.
kids: Children, a shepherd had a hundred sheep. One got lost! Did he say, “Never mind, I still have ninety-nine”? No! He searched and searched until he found it.
Then he carried it home on his shoulders and had a party! Jesus loves each of us like that.
Is there someone who feels left out in your class or family? How can you help them feel loved?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we honour two very different men. Peter, a fisherman from Galilee, impulsive and warm-hearted, who denied Jesus three times. Paul, an educated Pharisee, who persecuted the Church. Christ chose both, changed both, and both gave their lives in Rome.

At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asked: “Who do you say that I am?” Peter answered: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.” And Jesus said: “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom.” This is why we love and obey the Pope, Peter's successor. Our Malankara Church came into Catholic communion in 1930 precisely to be one with Peter.

But see how Peter's authority was born. After his denial, Jesus asked him three times: “Do you love me?” Peter answered: “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” And Jesus said: “Feed my sheep.” Authority in the Church is born from mercy and is exercised in love. A pope, a bishop, a priest, a parent: first love Jesus, then feed his sheep.

Paul, near his death, wrote: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” May each of us say that at the end of our life. Today, let us pray for Pope Leo, our Major Archbishop and our bishop, as the Church prayed fervently for Peter in prison. Sts Peter and Paul, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter was a fisherman. Jesus called him the Rock and made him the leader of the apostles. Today the Pope takes Peter's place!
Paul once hurt Christians, but Jesus met him and changed his heart. He travelled all over the world telling people about Jesus.
Jesus asked Peter: “Do you love me?” What would you answer? Let's say together: “Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, before Jesus sent out the seventy, he did not give them money or maps. He gave them a prayer: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.” Every vocation in the Church begins with someone praying. Somebody prayed for the priest who baptised you. Somebody is praying today for the priest who will one day anoint you.

Then Jesus said: “See, I am sending you out like lambs into the midst of wolves.” No purse, no bag, no sandals. They were to enter a house and first say, “Peace to this house!” Why so poor? So that people would see that the peace and the healing come from God, not from the messenger. Jericho fell not by weapons but by prayer and obedience. The Church grows the same way.

In Acts the apostles chose seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom to serve the tables, so that the apostles could give themselves to prayer and to the word. Every service in the parish matters: the one who teaches catechism, the one who cleans the church, the one who visits the sick. All of it is the work of the harvest. And all of it flows from the altar, where the one bread makes us one body.

The seventy came back rejoicing: even the demons obey us! Jesus said: rejoice rather that your names are written in heaven. Successes come and go; our name in the heart of God remains. This week, pray every day for vocations, bless the houses you enter with the peace of Christ, and prepare for the Apostles' Fast that begins on Wednesday. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent seventy friends to visit many towns. He told them to take no bag and no money, only his peace.
When they entered a house they said: “Peace to this house!” You can say that too, quietly in your heart, when you go into a house.
The friends came back very happy. Jesus said: be happy most of all because God knows your name in heaven. He knows your name too!

homily: Dear friends, today June begins. The rain has come, and our children are back at school. On this day of beginnings the Church gives us St Justin, a man who loved to study, who searched for the truth for many years, and who finally found it in Jesus Christ and gave his life for him.

St Paul tells Timothy that the Church is the household of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and bulwark of the truth (1 Timothy 3:15). The Church is our home, and she is also a pillar that holds the truth high so that everyone can see it. And what is that truth? Paul sings it: Without any doubt, the mystery of our religion is great: He was revealed in flesh, vindicated in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among Gentiles, believed in throughout the world, taken up in glory (1 Timothy 3:16).

In the Gospel the people ask Jesus, “Who are you?” (John 8:25). Jesus answers: When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). We learn who Jesus is when we look at the Cross. Justin learned it from the Scriptures, and when the judge in Rome told him to sacrifice to the gods, he and his companions said they wanted nothing more than to suffer for Jesus Christ. He died a martyr about the year 165.

St Justin also left us the oldest full description of the Sunday Eucharist: the readings, the homily, the prayers, the bread and wine, the great thanksgiving and the Amen of the people. It is what we do in every Holy Qurbono. So today let us ask two graces: a love of learning that leads us to the truth, and the courage to confess Jesus, the Truth in person, wherever we are. Amen.
kids: Children, are you happy to go back to school? New books, new bags, maybe a new umbrella for the rain! Today we remember St Justin. He was a student who never stopped asking questions. He wanted to know: who is God? Many teachers could not answer him. Then he read the Bible and found Jesus. Jesus is the answer to our biggest questions. So when you open your books this year, say a small prayer: Jesus, help me to learn, and help me to know you better.

homily: Dear friends, in these days the monsoon has come and our farmers are planting. A seedling in the mud does not look like much. But they plant in hope, because they know what will come. Today God's word tells us that he works the same way.

St Paul says: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God (1 Corinthians 1:18). Some people wanted miracles, others wanted clever arguments. God gave the world something nobody expected: his Son dying on a cross out of love. For God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength (1 Corinthians 1:25).

Jesus gives two pictures. The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in the garden; it grew and became a tree (Luke 13:19). And it is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened (Luke 13:21). The seed is tiny; the yeast is hidden. But they change everything, slowly, from inside.

So let us not despise small things. A prayer said every night, a Holy Qurbono on a weekday, a kind word, a small gift to the poor: these are seeds and yeast. We plant; God gives the growth. And let us make the sign of the Cross with faith, because the Cross, which looks like weakness, is the power of God. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever planted a seed? You put a tiny seed into the soil, you water it, and you wait. One day a little green shoot comes up! Jesus said God's kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that grows into a big plant where birds make their nests. Every time you say a prayer, share your snack, or help your mother, you are planting a little seed for God. Do not worry if it is small. God will make it grow.

homily: Dear friends, before the rains every family cleans the house. Today Jesus tells a story about a house that was swept clean but left empty. The unclean spirit came back, found it swept and put in order, and brought seven other spirits more evil than itself (Luke 11:25–26). A clean house is good. An empty house is dangerous.

St Paul tells us who must live in our house. Those who believe are the descendants of Abraham (Galatians 3:7). Abraham believed God, and God blessed him and promised that all the nations would be blessed in him. Then Paul says what Jesus has done: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us (Galatians 3:13). On the Cross he took our place.

And why? In order that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith (Galatians 3:14). The Cross sweeps the house clean, and the Holy Spirit comes to live in it. That happened at our Baptism. It happens again in every good confession.

So do not stop at sweeping. If you have given up something wrong, fill that place with something good: prayer, the word of God, the Holy Qurbono, service to others. A heart where the Holy Spirit lives has no room for the seven spirits. Amen.
kids: Children, does your family clean the house before the rainy season? Jesus told a story about a clean house where nobody lived. Because it was empty, the bad things came back! Your heart is like a house. When you say sorry to God, he cleans it. But then you must invite the Holy Spirit to live there, and fill your heart with good things: prayers, kind words, helping others. Then there is no room for the bad things to come back.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam asks us to remember Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, a bishop of our Church who went to the Lord in 2019. It is also the First Friday, and the Latin Church celebrates today the Sacred Heart of Jesus. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7).

Then it says: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). Bishops and priests come and go; the Lord who sends them remains. And Hebrews shows us where his love was poured out: Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood (Hebrews 13:12). There, on Calvary, a soldier pierced his side, and blood and water came out. That open Heart is the source of every shepherd's love.

The Gospel asks: Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household? (Matthew 24:45). A bishop is such a servant, but so is every father and mother, every teacher, every one of us who has someone to care for. Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46).

So today let us pray for the soul of Mar Timotheos and for all our shepherds. Let us bring our hearts to the Heart of Jesus in confession and Communion on this First Friday. And let us do what Hebrews asks: offer a sacrifice of praise, and do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God (Hebrews 13:16). Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember a bishop called Mar Timotheos, who has gone to be with Jesus. A bishop is like a shepherd who looks after God's people. But the best shepherd of all is Jesus. Jesus loves us so much that he gave his life for us on the Cross. Today is the First Friday, when many people remember the Heart of Jesus, full of love for us. You can give Jesus a gift from your heart today: share something with a friend, or say thank you to Jesus for loving you.

homily: Dear friends, today St Paul, old and in prison, writes to his young friend Timothy. He reminds him of everything he has seen and suffered, and he tells him: Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted (2 Timothy 3:12). But he also tells him where to find strength: in the people who taught him the faith, and in the Scriptures he has known from childhood.

Paul says: All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16). The Bible is breathed by God. It teaches us, it corrects us, and it makes us ready for every good work. That is why we listen to it in every Holy Qurbono, and why we should read it at home.

In the Gospel Jesus reads the Psalms and shows that they speak of him: David himself calls him Lord; so how can he be his son? (Mark 12:37). Jesus is the Son of David, but also David's Lord, the Son of God. And the large crowd was listening to him with delight (Mark 12:37). God's word is meant to bring us joy.

Today we remember St Boniface, who carried the Gospel from England to the German peoples and died a martyr in 754, holding, so tradition says, a book of the Gospels. Let us thank God for those who taught us the faith, let us read the Bible with delight, and let us hand it on to our children. Amen.
kids: Children, who taught you your first prayers? Maybe your grandmother, or your mother, or your teacher at Sunday school. St Paul's friend Timothy learned about God from his grandmother and his mother. Paul says that the Bible is breathed by God, like when God breathed life into Adam. Today we remember St Boniface, who loved the Bible so much that he carried it to faraway countries. Ask someone at home to read you a Bible story tonight, and listen with joy!

homily: Dear friends, today St Paul tells us how to pray: I desire, then, that in every place the men should pray, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument (1 Timothy 2:8). Our hands must be holy and our hearts must be at peace. We cannot shout at our family and then lift up our hands to God as if nothing had happened. That is why, in every Holy Qurbono, we give one another the peace before the great prayer of offering.
