Paul also asks Christians not to show off with gold and expensive clothes, but to be adorned with good works. That is a word for all of us, in a time of costly weddings and display. Some of Paul's words to the women of Ephesus are hard to hear today. The Church reads them in the light of all Scripture, which teaches that God created man and woman equal in dignity, in his own image. And the Church has always honoured the women who teach the faith: our mothers, our catechists, our sisters, and the women saints.

In the Gospel Jesus promises: the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you (John 14:26). The Holy Spirit helps the Church understand God's word. And Jesus gives a gift: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives (John 14:27).

So this week, let us lift up holy hands, let go of anger, make peace before we pray, and let the Holy Spirit teach us. And let us not be afraid, because the peace of Christ is stronger than any trouble. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever said your prayers while you were still angry with your brother or sister? It is hard to pray then, isn't it? St Paul says we should lift up our hands to God without anger. So first, say sorry and make peace. Jesus gives us a special gift: his peace. It is not just being quiet; it is a happy, calm feeling inside, because we know Jesus loves us. Tonight, before you pray, give a hug to anyone you were angry with today.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul says today: we know that a person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:16). That is good news for every one of us. We do not stand before God with a list of our achievements. We stand before him because Christ loved us and gave himself for us.

Paul also warns us: if I build up again the very things that I once tore down, then I demonstrate that I am a transgressor (Galatians 2:18). Grace pulled down our pride and the walls between us. Let us not build them up again by counting our good deeds or looking down on others.

In the Gospel Jesus promises the Holy Spirit: he will testify on my behalf. You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning (John 15:26–27). The Spirit speaks, and we speak; the Spirit works, and we work. Today we remember St Mariam Thresia of Puthenchira. She went into the homes of the sick, the poor and the troubled, and the Spirit testified to Jesus through her hands.

So let us receive God's grace with humility, and let us carry it into homes, beginning with our own. A visit, a meal, a prayer at a sickbed, a quarrel healed: this is how the Spirit testifies today. Amen.
kids: Children, do we have to earn God's love by being very good? No! God loves us first, and Jesus gave his life for us. That is a gift. Because we have received it, we want to share it. Today we remember St Mariam Thresia from Kerala. She loved Jesus so much that she went to visit sick people and poor families, and helped them. When you help your mother at home, or share with a friend who has nothing, you are telling people about Jesus without even using words.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul shows us today what happens when people turn away from God: they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25). When God is not at the centre, something else takes his place, and life slowly falls into disorder.

Paul's list of sins is long, and it includes all of us: gossips, slanderers, boastful, rebellious toward parents (Romans 1:29–30). We must not read this page and think of other people. Paul says in the next chapter: you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge others (Romans 2:1). We all need mercy.

And mercy comes. In the Gospel Jesus stands at the tomb of Lazarus. Martha says: even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him (John 11:22). Jesus answers: I am the resurrection and the life (John 11:25). He asks her, and he asks us: Do you believe this?

Let us answer with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God (John 11:27). Whatever has died in us, whatever we have lost by turning away, Jesus can raise. Let us put him back at the centre today, and let us trust him with our departed. Amen.
kids: Children, sometimes people love things more than they love God: toys, phones, money. St Paul says that when we put things in God's place, everything goes wrong. In the Gospel, Jesus' friend Lazarus had died, and his sister Martha was crying. Jesus told her: I am the resurrection and the life. Jesus is stronger than death! Let us always keep Jesus in the first place in our hearts, and he will keep us safe for ever.

homily: Dear friends, today St Paul introduces us to a man most of us hardly know: Epaphroditus. Paul calls him my brother and co-worker and fellow soldier, your messenger and minister to my need (Philippians 2:25). The Philippians had sent him to help Paul in prison, and he became so ill that he nearly died.

Paul says: Welcome him then in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people (Philippians 2:29). Every parish is held up by people like Epaphroditus, catechists, sacristans, those who care for the sick, those who clean and arrange. This month the schools reopen, and many teachers and staff will work hard for our children. Let us honour such people, and thank them.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth (John 16:12–13). The Holy Spirit is a patient teacher. He teaches the Church through the centuries, and he teaches each of us through our lives, step by step.

So let us stay in his school. Let us keep coming to the Holy Qurbono, keep reading the word, keep praying, even when we do not understand everything. And let us be co-workers like Epaphroditus, giving ourselves for the work of Christ without asking for honour. Amen.
kids: Children, schools are opening again! Your teachers will help you learn new things, a little at a time. Jesus said that the Holy Spirit is like a teacher too: he helps us understand God a little more every day. Today we also heard about Epaphroditus, a helper of St Paul who worked so hard that he became sick. St Paul said: honour people like him. Who helps you every day? Your parents, your teachers, your bus driver? Say thank you to them this week!

homily: Dear friends, today is a family feast for our Church. On 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI erected the hierarchy of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church, with the Archeparchy of Thiruvananthapuram and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla. Two years before, in 1930, Mar Ivanios, Mar Theophilos and a few companions had entered full communion with the Catholic Church, leaving buildings and properties behind, but keeping our beautiful liturgy and the faith of our fathers.

St Paul tells us today: since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). And he tells us the source of it all: God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us (Romans 5:5). Our Church was born from that love, and from a longing for reconciliation and unity.

In the Gospel Jesus promises: I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you (John 14:18). And again: we will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:23). Through our bishops in communion with the successor of Peter, through the sacraments and through the faith they guard, the Lord keeps that promise. Our Church is meant to be a home where God lives and where every one of us belongs.

Today the Panchangam also remembers two apostles. Mar Barthulmai, Bartholomew, one of the Twelve, whom many identify with Nathanael, the Israelite in whom there is no deceit. And Mar Barnabas, son of encouragement, who stood by Saul when others were afraid, and who was set apart by the Holy Spirit at Antioch while the church was praying and fasting.

So on this day let us thank God for our Church, pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our bishops, and pray for the unity of all Christians, especially our brothers and sisters of the other Malankara Churches. And let us be like Barnabas: people who encourage, who open the door, who make the Church a home. Amen.
kids: Children, today is like a birthday for our Malankara Catholic Church! In 1932 the Pope gave our Church its own bishops and its own dioceses, so that we would have a home in the big family of the Catholic Church. Jesus said: I will not leave you alone like orphans. We also remember two friends of Jesus: Bartholomew, who never told lies, and Barnabas, who always encouraged people. When a new child comes to your class or your Sunday school, be a Barnabas: smile, sit with them and help them feel at home.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul begins today with words from his heart: Brothers and sisters, my heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved (Romans 10:1). He is speaking of his own people, Israel. Paul loved them all his life, and the Church teaches us to speak of the Jewish people with reverence and gratitude, for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

Paul says that some had a zeal for God, but it is not enlightened (Romans 10:2). They were trying to establish their own righteousness. That danger is ours too. We can pray and fast and serve to make ourselves important. But Christ is the end of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes (Romans 10:4). We receive righteousness from him.

In the Gospel a father kneels before Jesus: Lord, have mercy on my son (Matthew 17:15). The disciples could not heal the boy, but Jesus did. Then Jesus tells them: if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move (Matthew 17:20). A small faith, a real faith, is enough, because God is great.

Next Wednesday we begin the Apostles' Fast. Let us keep it humbly, not to make ourselves righteous, but to open our hearts to Christ. Let us bring our children and our families to Jesus by name, and pray for the salvation of those we love. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever seen a mustard seed? It is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice! Jesus said that if we have faith even as small as a mustard seed, God can do great things through us. In the Gospel a father brought his sick son to Jesus, and Jesus made him well. When someone in your family is sick or sad, bring them to Jesus in your prayers. Your faith may be small, but God is very big!

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam remembers Elisha the Prophet. He was ploughing his field when Elijah threw his mantle over him, and he left everything to follow. Before Elijah was taken up, Elisha asked: Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit (2 Kings 2:9). God gave it, and Elisha's life was full of mercy: oil for a poor widow, a child raised to life, bread for the hungry, healing for a foreign soldier.

In the Gospel Jesus reminds the people of Nazareth: there were also many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian (Luke 4:27). God's mercy reached beyond the borders people expected. The people were filled with rage, but he passed through the midst of them and went on his way (Luke 4:30). Nothing can stop the mercy of God.

St Paul shows us what that mercy does in us: present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and present your members to God as instruments of righteousness (Romans 6:13). Like Naaman in the Jordan, we went down into the water of Baptism and came up clean. Now our eyes, our tongues, our hands and our feet belong to God.

On Wednesday the Apostles' Fast begins. Let us decide now what we will offer: a meal, a habit, our time, our care for a stranger. Let us ask, like Elisha, for a double share of the Spirit, and let us offer our bodies to God as instruments of his righteousness. Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember Elisha, a prophet who helped many people with God's power. A soldier called Naaman was very sick, and a little girl in his house told his wife about Elisha. Naaman went to the river Jordan, washed seven times, and was healed! Jesus said God loves people from every country. On Wednesday our Church begins the Apostles' Fast. You can give something to God too: maybe kind words, sharing your snacks, or saying your prayers without being told.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam remembers the founding of the first church built in the name of the holy Mother of God. We do not know where it stood. But we know its children: so many churches in our land carry her name. And the Gospel today is about worship. Jesus says to the Samaritan woman: the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth (John 4:23).

Worship in spirit and truth is not prayer without a church. The Spirit is the Holy Spirit of Pentecost, and the Truth is Jesus himself, who says: I am he, the one who is speaking to you (John 4:26). We worship in spirit and truth above all when we gather at the altar for the Holy Qurbono. The church building is not a box for God. Solomon said that heaven itself cannot contain him (1 Kings 8:27). The church is a home for God's family.

Why name a church after Mary? Because she was the first house of God among us. The Word of God lived in her womb. A church with her name does not take us away from Jesus. Mary says what she said at Cana: do whatever he tells you (John 2:5).

And St Paul adds: in whatever condition you were called, brothers and sisters, there remain with God (1 Corinthians 7:24). Our worship must not stay inside the church. Like the holy Mother of God in her house at Nazareth, let us make our homes, our fields, our offices and our classrooms places where God is honoured. Amen.
kids: Children, what is the name of your parish church? Many churches in Kerala are named after Mother Mary. Do you know why? Because Mary was the very first home of Jesus. Before any church was built, Jesus lived inside his mother, close to her heart. Today Jesus tells us that God loves people who pray with true hearts. So when you go to church, pray with all your heart. And at home, before you study or play, say a little prayer too. Then your home also becomes a small church.

homily: Dear friends, today the Apostles' Fast begins, and it will end with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul. Jesus said that when the bridegroom is taken away, his friends will fast (Matthew 9:15). The Lord has gone up to the Father and the Spirit has come. Now, like the apostles, we fast and pray so that the Church may go out with the Good News.

In the Gospel Jesus calls the Twelve and gives them authority over unclean spirits and every sickness (Matthew 10:1). Then we hear their names: Peter and Andrew, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew, James and Thaddaeus, Simon, and Judas who betrayed him (Matthew 10:2–4). Our own Mar Thoma is among them. Jesus does not choose an idea; he chooses persons. Our bishops are their successors today, and in this fast we pray for them.

St Paul says: think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries (1 Corinthians 4:1). A steward takes care of what belongs to his master. The holy mysteries do not belong to the priest; he holds them in trust. And we too are stewards of our time, our money and our faith. Fasting teaches us this. It is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy (1 Corinthians 4:2).

Paul also warns: do not pronounce judgment before the time (1 Corinthians 4:5). A fast that makes us harsh with others is not the fast of the apostles. So let us fast humbly, pray for our shepherds, give what we save to the poor, and leave judgment to the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, today a special time of prayer begins: the Apostles' Fast. The apostles were Jesus' twelve special friends. He called each one by his name, Peter, John, Thomas and the others, and sent them to tell the whole world about God. Before they went, they prayed and fasted. During these days you can give up one sweet or one cartoon, and pray for our bishop and our priest. And the money you save for a chocolate can go to a child who needs it. That is how we help the apostles' work today.

homily: Dear friends, the monsoon has come, and today Jesus speaks about floods. He tells of two builders. One dug deeply and laid the foundation on rock; when a flood arose, the river burst against that house but could not shake it (Luke 6:48). The other built without a foundation, and immediately it fell (Luke 6:49). Both men heard the words of Jesus. Only one acted on them.

Jesus asks a hard question: why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you? (Luke 6:46). We can come to church, sing well and know many prayers, and still be building on sand, if the word of God never reaches our daily choices. Hearing is not enough. We must dig deeply.

St Paul tells us what the rock is. Continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith (Colossians 2:6–7). Christ is the rock. In Baptism we were buried with him and raised with him. And God took the record of our sins and set it aside, nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:14). Our foundation is not our own strength but what Christ has done for us.

In this Apostles' Fast, let us dig deeply. Let us find one word of Jesus that we hear but do not live, and live it. And when the rain falls at night, let us remember to pray for those whose homes are in danger. A house built on Christ will stand. Amen.
kids: Children, have you seen how strong the water is in the monsoon? It can carry away mud, trees and even houses. Jesus told a story about two houses. One was built on a big rock, and when the flood came it stood strong. The other was built on soft ground, and it fell down with a crash! Jesus says: if you listen to me and do what I say, you are like the house on the rock. So when Jesus says, be kind, share, forgive, let us really do it. Then we will be strong like that house.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Mar Aprem Malpan, St Ephrem the Syrian. He was a deacon in Nisibis and Edessa in the fourth century, and he wrote hundreds of hymns that taught the faith. Our Syriac tradition calls him the Harp of the Spirit, and the whole Church honours him as a Doctor.

The Epistle says that the law has only a shadow of the good things to come (Hebrews 10:1). The old sacrifices pointed forward, but it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins (Hebrews 10:4). Only Jesus, by his one offering, takes away sin. Mar Aprem loved to find these shadows and symbols in Scripture and in nature, and to show how all of them point to Christ.

And what do they point to? To friendship. Jesus says: I do not call you servants any longer, but I have called you friends (John 15:15). No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends (John 15:13). On the Cross, Jesus made us his friends. And friends of Jesus must love one another as he loved us.

Mar Aprem was such a friend. He prayed, fasted, sang and, when famine came, cared for the hungry. In this Apostles' Fast, let us ask him to teach us to see Christ in the Scriptures, to praise him with joy, and to love one another in deeds. Amen.
kids: Children, do you like to sing? Today we remember a saint who loved to sing about Jesus: Mar Aprem. He lived long, long ago and wrote many, many songs to teach people about Jesus and Mother Mary. People called him the harp of the Holy Spirit, because his songs were like music played by God. Jesus says today: you are my friends. A friend of Jesus sings his praises and helps others. So today, sing a hymn for Jesus, and help someone who needs you.

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews tells us what Jesus said when he came into the world: a body you have prepared for me; then I said, ‘See, God, I have come to do your will, O God’ (Hebrews 10:5, 7). Jesus took a body from the Virgin Mary to offer it for us. And it is by God's will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all (Hebrews 10:10).

In the Gospel Jesus shows what doing the Father's will means. You have heard, an eye for an eye; but I say to you, do not resist an evildoer; turn the other cheek; go also the second mile (Matthew 5:38–41). Jesus is not saying that evil does not matter. He is teaching us to stop the chain of revenge. And he goes even further: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). That is what he did on the Cross.

Today we remember Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, St Jude, one of the Twelve. At the Last Supper he asked: Lord, how is it that you will reveal yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered: those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:22–23). Many people today come to St Jude with problems that seem hopeless. He points them to the God who makes his home in us.

In this Apostles' Fast, let us fast also from revenge. Let us pray for someone who has hurt us, go the second mile for someone who does not deserve it, and bring our hardest intentions to the Lord with St Jude. Amen.
kids: Children, what do you do when someone pushes you or says something bad to you? It is easy to push back. But Jesus says: do not hit back; be kind instead, and pray for that person. That is very hard! But Jesus did it on the Cross, when he prayed for the people who hurt him. Today we also remember St Jude, a friend of Jesus. Many people ask St Jude to pray for them when they have big problems. Tonight, say a prayer for someone who was not kind to you. Jesus will be very happy.

homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel Jesus asks his disciples: what were you arguing about on the way? (Mark 9:33). They were silent, because they had argued about who was the greatest (Mark 9:34). Jesus had just told them that he would suffer and die, and they were thinking about their own importance.

Jesus sat down and said: whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all (Mark 9:35). Then he took a little child in his arms and said: whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me (Mark 9:37). A child had no importance in that world. Jesus puts the least in the centre, and says that we find him there.

St Paul asks: whom are you serving? If you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness (Romans 6:16). Every life serves something. In this Apostles' Fast, let us look at our eyes, our tongue, our hands and our time, and give them to God.

Today we remember St Aloysius Gonzaga. He was the heir of a noble family, but he left everything to serve God. In 1591 he carried the sick of Rome on his shoulders, caught the plague and died at twenty-three. He chose to be last and servant of all. As schools and colleges reopen, let us pray for our students, that they may learn not only to be first, but to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever argued about who is the best, who is the fastest or who gets the first turn? The disciples of Jesus did that too! Jesus told them: the most important person is the one who helps everyone. Then he hugged a little child and said: when you are kind to a child, you are kind to me. Today we remember St Aloysius, who was rich and could have been a prince, but he chose to help sick people. As school starts again, try to be the one who helps, not the one who wants to be first.

homily: Dear friends, we are keeping the Apostles' Fast, and the Church reminds us that fasting has two companions: prayer and almsgiving. Today St Paul speaks of giving, and he uses the picture of a farmer: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). In these rainy weeks our farmers are sowing. Nobody sows a handful and hopes to fill a granary.

Paul goes on: each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). God does not ask for a gift squeezed out of us with a sigh. He looks for a heart that gives gladly, because it has learned from him. And he promises that the giver will not run dry: God is able to provide you with every blessing in abundance (2 Corinthians 9:8).

Jesus goes deeper still. Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and where thieves break in and steal (Matthew 6:19). Store them up in heaven. And he tells us why it matters so much: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Matthew 6:21). What we hold on to holds on to us.

So in these days of the fast, let us put aside what we save, a meal, a treat, a little spending, and give it with a smile to someone who needs it. That is seed sown for a harvest, and treasure sent ahead to heaven. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what a farmer does when the rain comes? He takes his seeds and throws them into the wet field. The seeds seem to disappear, but after some weeks green plants come up, and later there is a big harvest! St Paul says that when we share, it is like sowing seeds. What we give is not lost; it grows. And God loves people who share with a happy face. This week, share something with a smile: a snack, a pencil, a toy, or your time.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul ends his Letter to the Ephesians by sending a friend: Tychicus, a dear brother and a faithful minister in the Lord (Ephesians 6:21). Paul sends him to let you know how we are, and to encourage your hearts (Ephesians 6:22). The Church grows through the great Apostles, and also through quiet helpers like Tychicus. Every parish has them, and we thank God for them.

In the Gospel, the man born blind has been healed, but instead of rejoicing with him, people argue and throw him out. Then Jesus heard that they had driven him out, and when he found him, he said, Do you believe in the Son of Man? (John 9:35). The man answers: Tell me, so that I may believe in him (John 9:36). And when Jesus shows himself, he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshiped him (John 9:38).

Then Jesus speaks of another blindness. Some said: Surely we are not blind, are we? (John 9:40). And Jesus answers that if they admitted their blindness, they could be healed; but now that you say, We see, your sin remains (John 9:41). The most dangerous blindness is the one that refuses to admit it is blind.

In this Apostles' Fast, let us ask the Lord to show us what we do not see, and let us go to confession. Let us look for those who are left out, as Jesus did. And let us say with our whole heart, and with our knees: Lord, I believe. Amen.
kids: Children, close your eyes for a moment. Now open them. What do you see? The man in today's Gospel could not see anything from the day he was born. Jesus healed him, and then Jesus came to find him again. When the man understood who Jesus was, he said: Lord, I believe! and he knelt down. When you come into the church and see the tabernacle, you can kneel and whisper the same words: Jesus, I believe in you.

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate a birthday. The Church keeps the birthday of very few saints, but she keeps the birth of John the Baptist, because his birth was part of the good news. Before he was born he was filled with the Holy Spirit, and when the Mother of God came to visit Elizabeth, the child leaped in her womb (Luke 1:41).

St Luke tells us that when Elizabeth bore a son, her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her (Luke 1:58). Then they wanted to name the child after his father. But Elizabeth said: No; he is to be called John (Luke 1:60). And Zechariah, who had been silent for months, asked for a writing tablet and wrote, His name is John (Luke 1:63). At once his mouth was opened and he began to speak, praising God (Luke 1:64). Obedience opened his lips, and his first words were praise.

The people asked: What then will this child become? For, indeed, the hand of the Lord was with him (Luke 1:66). John became the voice in the desert, the man of fasting and prayer who prepared the way of the Lord and pointed his own disciples to Jesus. Some of the Apostles were first his disciples. In this Apostles' Fast we thank God for him.

The Epistle tells us how to follow him: Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14). Do not be like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal (Hebrews 12:16). Today we also remember Cheppattu Philipose Ramban and all who spoke the word of God to us. Let us imitate their faith, let us pray for our children, and let us say with John: He must increase, but I must decrease. Amen.
kids: Children, today is the birthday of John the Baptist! His parents were very old, and God gave them a baby as a surprise. Everyone wanted to call him by his father's name, but God had chosen the name John. His father wrote it on a little board: His name is John! When John grew up, he told everyone: Look, there is Jesus, the Lamb of God! You have just begun a new school year. Like John, you can help your friends to know Jesus, by being kind and by praying for them.

homily: Dear friends, today the Letter to the Hebrews tells us: By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac (Hebrews 11:17). It was the hardest test of his life. Isaac was the son of the promise. But Abraham trusted, because he considered the fact that God is able even to raise someone from the dead (Hebrews 11:19). On this Friday we think of the Father who gave his own Son for us, and raised him from the dead.

Then the letter speaks of old men blessing their children: by faith Isaac invoked blessings for the future on Jacob and Esau (Hebrews 11:20), and Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph (Hebrews 11:21). They did not see the promise fulfilled, but they passed it on. Our elders still bless children with the sign of the cross before school and before journeys. That is the faith of the patriarchs living in our homes.

In the Gospel, people are amazed at the teaching of Jesus. He says: My teaching is not mine but his who sent me. Anyone who resolves to do the will of God will know whether the teaching is from God (John 7:16–17). If we want to understand our faith, we must begin by living it. Then Jesus adds: Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment (John 7:24).

So on this Friday of the fast, let us ask for a faith that trusts in hard times, a faith that blesses the next generation, and a heart that does not judge by appearances. Let us bless our children, and let us look at every person as God looks at them. Amen.
kids: Children, does your grandmother or your mother make a little cross on your forehead before you go to school? That is a blessing! Long ago, Isaac and Jacob, who were very old, also blessed their children and grandchildren and asked God to take care of them. And Jesus tells us something important: do not judge people by how they look. A new boy or girl in your class may look different, but God loves them very much. Be kind to them!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul thanks the Philippians for their help: no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving, except you alone (Philippians 4:15). They were not a rich church, but they kept supporting the apostle so that the gospel could go further. Tomorrow is Seminary Day, and we will be asked to help the seminary where young men are formed to be priests. That is our way of sharing in the gospel, as the Philippians did.

Paul calls their gift a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God (Philippians 4:18). And he makes a promise: my God will fully satisfy every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:19). No one becomes truly poor by giving to God.

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks hard words to those who were opposing him, and he warns about the devil, who is a liar and the father of lies (John 8:44). These words are not a judgement on a people; they are a warning to every heart. And Jesus gives us a sign of those who belong to God: Whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47).

So let us do two things. Let us give generously tomorrow for the seminary and pray for our future priests. And for the rest of this Apostles' Fast, let us keep the fast of the tongue: no lies, no gossip, no rumours passed on. Let us listen to the word of God and speak the truth in love. Amen.
kids: Children, a long time ago the Christians of a town called Philippi sent presents to St Paul so that he could keep going from place to place telling people about Jesus. Tomorrow our Church will collect money for the seminary, the big school where young men learn to become priests. You can bring a coin too! And Jesus tells us today that God's children always tell the truth. If you have told a lie, say sorry, and try to always speak the truth.

homily: Dear friends, today is the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast, and tomorrow we celebrate Sts Peter and Paul. St Paul writes to Timothy: avoid wrangling over words, which does no good but only ruins those who are listening (2 Timothy 2:14). Instead, be a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth (2 Timothy 2:15). Quarrels about words destroy; the truth explained with love builds up.

Today we remember Mar Irenaeus. As a young man he listened to St Polycarp, who had known the Apostle John. He became bishop of Lyons and defended the faith against people who invented secret teachings. He told them: look at the faith handed down in the Church from the Apostles, and especially in the Church of Rome founded on Peter and Paul. His name means peaceful, and he worked for peace among the churches. We also pray today for our bishop Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Apostles: You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). The fruit has lasted: from John to Polycarp to Irenaeus, and down to us. And Jesus tells us what that fruit is: I am giving you these commands so that you may love one another (John 15:17).

So let us thank God for those who handed on the faith to us. Let us learn our faith well, so that we can explain it straight. Let us avoid quarrels that wound, and let us prepare our hearts for tomorrow's feast. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever played the game where you whisper a message from one person to the next? Sometimes the message gets mixed up! Jesus gave his message to the Apostles, and they passed it on very carefully. St Irenaeus learned it from Polycarp, who learned it from the Apostle John. And it came all the way to us, through our parents and teachers. Listen well when you learn about Jesus, so that you can pass the message on without mixing it up.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated Sts Peter and Paul, and today we remember all twelve Apostles together. St Mark tells us: He went up the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him (Mark 3:13). St Luke says that Jesus first spent the night in prayer (Luke 6:12). The Apostles were born from the prayer of Jesus.

Why did he choose them? Mark answers: he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message (Mark 3:14). First, to be with him. Then, to be sent. We cannot give Jesus to others if we have not spent time with him. And if we really have been with him, we cannot keep him to ourselves.

The Twelve were very different: fishermen, a tax collector, fiery brothers, quiet men. Among them was Thomas, who came to our land and whose Dukhrono we keep on Saturday. St Paul tells us what the apostolic life costs and what it gives: as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). And he reminds us: now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation (2 Corinthians 6:2).

The Apostles' Fast is over, but the mission continues. Our bishops, with the successor of Peter, carry on the work of the Twelve, and every one of us is called in our own way. So let us be with Jesus each day in prayer and in the Holy Qurbono, and let us go where he sends us. Holy Apostles of the Lord, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once went up a mountain and called twelve friends to be his Apostles. Can you count them on your fingers? Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James, Thaddaeus, Simon and Judas. They were all different, but Jesus loved each one. First he wanted them to be with him, and then he sent them to tell others about God. Jesus wants you to be with him too, when you pray, and then to go and be kind to others in his name.

intro: Theme: “Sent two by two, fed by the Bread of Life.”
Rejected in his hometown, Jesus does not stop; he sends the Twelve two by two. In John he says: “I am the bread of life.” The three young men in Daniel show the courage of faith that refuses idols.

points.h: Come to the Bread of Life
sub: Isaiah invites the thirsty and the poor to come and eat freely.
Jesus says: whoever comes to me will never hunger; I will never drive away anyone who comes.
In the Holy Qurbono that invitation is fulfilled.
q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat!
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.”
points.apply: Prepare well for your next Holy Communion with a few minutes of silent prayer.

sub: “Two are better than one”: mission is done in communion, not alone.
Jesus sends the Twelve with authority; they preach repentance, cast out demons and anoint the sick.
The Church sees here a hint of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
q: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up the other.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.
points.apply: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with a family member or friend.

points.h: Faith that will not bow to idols
sub: The three young men: “Our God is able to deliver us … but if not, we will not serve your gods.”
Mature faith does not bargain with God.
St Paul boasts only in the Cross, and in being a new creation.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire … let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
points.apply: Name one modern “golden statue” (money, status, screens) and refuse to bow to it this week.

concl: Fed by Christ, sent together, faithful to the end: this is the Church after Pentecost.
Let us come to the Bread of Life and go out to share it.
2027-06-06.resolve: Pray for the Syro-Malankara Church on the anniversary of its hierarchy (11 June 1932).

intro: Theme: “You give them something to eat.”

Jesus feeds the crowd through the hands of his disciples, teaches them that greatness is service, and calls unexpected instruments like Saul. This Sunday we pray especially for priests and seminarians.

sub: Through Elijah God kept the widow's jar of meal and jug of oil from running out.
Jesus blesses and breaks five loaves and gives them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
Every priest at the altar continues this: Christ feeds his people through human hands.
q: The jar of meal was not emptied, neither did the jug of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by Elijah.
And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd. And all ate and were filled.
points.apply: Pray by name for the priests who serve your parish.

sub: God told Jeremiah: before you were born I consecrated you.
He chose Saul, a persecutor, as his instrument, and sent Ananias to lay hands on him.
Vocations are God's gift and the Church's task: families and seminaries form those he calls.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But the Lord said to him, “Go, for he is an instrument whom I have chosen to bring my name before Gentiles and kings and before the people of Israel.”
points.apply: Encourage a young person to consider whether God is calling them.

points.h: Servant of all, renewed in strength
sub: The disciples argue about greatness; Jesus places a child in their midst.
“Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
Those who serve grow weary; God gives power to the faint.
q: Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
points.apply: Serve someone at home this week without being asked.

concl: Christ multiplies what we give and feeds the world through servants.
Let us pray for our priests, offer our five loaves, and serve with joy.
2027-06-20.resolve: Offer a day of prayer and fasting this week for seminarians.

intro: Theme: “The Shepherd who searches, the body that belongs together.”
Jesus tells of the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine to find the one lost sheep. Paul reminds us that we are many members of one body. The apostles pray: “Increase our faith.”

points.h: The Shepherd searches for the lost
sub: Through Ezekiel God promised to seek the lost himself.
Jesus fulfils it: he goes after the one sheep until he finds it and carries it home on his shoulders.
Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents; the Sacrament of Reconciliation is that joy today.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak.

Which one of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it? When he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices.
points.apply: Pray for one person who has drifted from the Church, and reach out to them gently.

sub: Paul: the body is one though its members are many; no member can say “I have no need of you.”
The weaker members are indispensable; when one suffers, all suffer.
Family and parish are where this unity is lived first.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Now the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one claimed private ownership of any possessions, but everything they owned was held in common.
points.apply: Thank a family member or parishioner whose quiet service is often unnoticed.

sub: God's plans stand firm; nothing can overturn them.
Faith the size of a mustard seed is enough, because its power is God's.
Having done all, we say: “We are worthless slaves; we have done only what we ought to have done.” Humility guards faith.
q: The LORD of hosts has sworn: As I have designed, so shall it be; and as I have planned, so shall it come to pass.

The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!” The Lord replied, “If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.”
points.apply: Each day this week pray the apostles' prayer: “Lord, increase my faith.”

concl: The Shepherd seeks us, the body holds us, and faith keeps us humble and strong.
Let us return to him, belong to one another, and serve without seeking reward.
2027-06-27.resolve: Make a good confession before the feast of St Thomas.

intro: Theme: “The Rock and the Runner.”

Today the Apostles' Fast ends with the feast of the two pillars of the Church. Peter confesses Christ and receives the keys; Paul runs the race to the end. One was a fisherman, the other a persecutor. Christ made both apostles, and both were martyred in Rome.

points.h: Peter: the confession and the rock
sub: “Who do you say that I am?” Peter answers: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus names him Peter, the rock, and gives him the keys of the kingdom.
The Church rests on Christ and on the faith Peter confessed; Peter's ministry continues in the Bishop of Rome, with whom our Church is in full communion.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
points.apply: Pray today for Pope Leo XIV and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos.

sub: Peter denied the Lord three times; by the lake he is asked three times, “Do you love me?”
Each answer of love becomes a mission: “Feed my sheep.”
Authority in the Church is born of love and is exercised as shepherding, as God promised through Ezekiel.
q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.

He said to him the third time, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Peter felt hurt because he said to him the third time, “Do you love me?” And he said to him, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.”
points.apply: Where you have failed the Lord, tell him again simply: “Lord, you know that I love you.”

sub: Like Daniel, who resolved not to defile himself, Paul held firm.
From persecutor to apostle: grace changed his whole life's direction.
At the end he could say he had fought the good fight and kept the faith.
q: But Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the royal rations of food and wine; so he asked the palace master to allow him not to defile himself.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
points.apply: Choose one area of life where you need perseverance and offer it to God today.

concl: Different temperaments, one faith, one Lord, one martyrdom.
Like Peter and Paul, let us confess Christ, love him after our falls, and run to the end.
2027-06-29.resolve: Read Acts 12:6–19 with your family and pray for the Church's shepherds.

intro: Theme: “Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
The Lord sends out the seventy: mission begins with prayer, travels light, serves the word and the table, and finds its joy in belonging to God.

points.h: Ask the Lord of the harvest
sub: Before any instruction, Jesus gives the seventy a prayer.
The harvest belongs to the Lord, and so do the labourers.
Every vocation in the Church begins with someone praying.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”
points.apply: Each day this week pray for one priest, one religious and one young person who may be called.

sub: No purse, no bag, no sandals: the messenger carries little so the message is seen clearly.
Their first word in every house is peace.
Jericho fell by obedience and prayer, not by weapons.
q: And at the seventh time, when the priests had blown the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city.”
Whatever house you enter, first say, “Peace to this house!”
points.apply: When you enter a home this week, bless it silently: Peace to this house.

points.h: Servants of the word and of the table
sub: The apostles choose seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom.
Prayer and the ministry of the word go together with service.
God preserves his servants as the vine-grower spares the cluster with a blessing in it.
q: Thus says the LORD: As the wine is found in the cluster, and they say, “Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,” so I will do for my servants' sake, and not destroy them all.

Therefore, friends, select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this task, while we, for our part, will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word.
points.apply: Offer one hour of service to your parish this month: catechism, choir, the sick or the poor.

points.h: Rejoice that your names are written in heaven
sub: The seventy return rejoicing that even the demons submit.
Jesus points them to a deeper joy.
Success in ministry passes; belonging to God remains.
q: O LORD, who may abide in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy hill?
Nevertheless, do not rejoice at this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
points.apply: Thank God tonight that he knows you by name.

concl: The harvest is the Lord's; pray, go in peace, and serve.
Our deepest joy is that God has written our names in heaven.
2027-06-13.resolve: Prepare now for the Apostles' Fast from 16 June: daily prayer for vocations and for the Church's mission.

intro: Theme: “Without any doubt, the mystery of our religion is great.”

On Tuesday of the second week after Pentecost, the memory of St Justin: the Church as the household and pillar of the truth, the great mystery of Christ, and the One lifted up who answers the question “Who are you?”

points.h: The household of God, the pillar of truth
sub: A home, not a club.
A pillar holds the truth up to be seen.
A bulwark keeps it from being knocked down.
q: The sum of your word is truth; and every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever.
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.
points.apply: When you hear the Church mocked this week, answer with one calm and true sentence instead of joining in or staying silent.

sub: Revealed in flesh.
Proclaimed among Gentiles, believed in throughout the world.
Taken up in glory.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Learn by heart the six lines of 1 Timothy 3:16 this week and pray them slowly each night.

points.h: “Who are you?”: the One lifted up
sub: Jesus answers from the Cross.
St Justin searched and found.
The philosopher who died for the Truth.
q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
points.apply: Spend five minutes before a crucifix this week and let Jesus answer the question: Who are you for me?

concl: The Church holds up the truth like a pillar, and the truth she holds up is a person: Christ revealed in flesh and lifted up on the Cross.
St Justin looked for him in every school and found him in the Scriptures, and gave his life for him.
2027-06-01.resolve: Love learning, seek in it the One who is the Truth, and confess him without fear.

intro: Theme: “For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.”
On Wednesday of the second week after Pentecost, in the season of monsoon sowing: the foolishness of the Cross, the mustard seed and the yeast, and God's small and hidden ways.

sub: Signs and wisdom: two honest hungers.
God answers both in Christ crucified.
Twelve fishermen and the cities of the world.
q: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the Lord.
May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
points.apply: Put a small cross where you will see it at your desk or in your shop, and look at it when you are tempted to trust only in cleverness or money.

sub: The smallest of beginnings.
Growth is God's work.
Room in its branches for the birds.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.
points.apply: Begin one small, regular good practice this week (a daily decade of the Rosary, a weekly visit to a lonely person) and keep it up.

sub: Hidden but active.
It changes the whole batch.
A Christian in an office, a classroom, a family.
q: For whoever has despised the day of small things shall rejoice
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Choose one place where you spend much time (work, school, a WhatsApp group) and be quietly kind and honest there all this week.

concl: God works like a farmer in June: he plants what looks small and foolish, and waits for the harvest.
The Cross, the seed and the yeast all say the same thing: trust his hidden power.
2027-06-02.resolve: Do not despise small things: plant, knead, and leave the growth to God.

intro: Theme: “So that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.”
On Thursday of the second week after Pentecost: children of Abraham through faith, Christ who became a curse for us, and the swept house that must be filled by the Spirit.

sub: Abraham believed, before the Law was given.
The Gospel announced beforehand: all nations blessed.
We are his children when we believe.
q: And he believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Take one step this week that you have put off because you could not see where it would lead, trusting God as Abraham did.

points.h: Christ became a curse for us
sub: The one who hung on the tree.
He took our punishment, not our guilt.
He gives us what is his.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
points.apply: On Friday make a short visit to a church or a wayside cross and thank Christ, by name, for one burden he has carried for you.

points.h: The swept house must not stay empty
sub: Getting rid of evil is not enough.
The Spirit comes to dwell.
Fill the empty room with good.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
but be filled with the Spirit,
points.apply: Name one habit you have given up, and choose one good practice to put firmly in its place this week.

concl: The Cross sweeps the house clean; the Holy Spirit comes to live in it.
A heart where the Spirit dwells has no room for the seven spirits.
2027-06-03.resolve: Do not stop at sweeping: let the Holy Spirit move in and fill your heart with good.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”

On Friday of the second week after Pentecost, the memory of Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, the First Friday, and the day the Latin Church keeps the Sacred Heart: remembering our shepherds, the Heart pierced outside the gate, and the faithful steward.

sub: Those who spoke the word of God to us.
Consider the outcome; imitate the faith.
Shepherds pass; the Shepherd remains.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will win the crown of glory that never fades away.
points.apply: Write down this week the name of one bishop, priest or catechist who gave you the faith, and one thing in them you want to imitate.

points.h: Outside the gate: the pierced Heart
sub: Jesus suffered outside the city gate.
Blood and water from the opened side.
We have an altar: praise and sharing.
q: so that, when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Keep the First Friday this month and the next with confession, Communion and one act of sharing.

sub: Put in charge of the household.
Food at the proper time.
Found at work when the master comes.
q: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
points.apply: Name the people the Lord has put in your care, and do one faithful, unnoticed act of care for each this week.

concl: We remember our shepherds and pray for them, and their memory sends us to the Heart of the Good Shepherd, pierced outside the gate.
From that Heart comes the strength to be faithful stewards in the household of God.
2027-06-04.resolve: Imitate the faith of your shepherds, bring your heart to the Heart of Jesus, and be found faithful at work.

intro: Theme: “All scripture is inspired by God.”
On Saturday of the second week after Pentecost, the memory of St Boniface: continuing in what we have learned, the God-breathed Scriptures, and Christ who is both David's son and David's Lord.

points.h: Continue in what you have learned
sub: Knowing from whom you learned it.
Lois, Eunice and our own grandmothers.
Steady in persecution.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Set a fixed time this week for the family to read a passage of Scripture together, even for five minutes.

sub: For teaching and reproof.
For correction and training in righteousness.
Equipped for every good work.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
because no prophecy ever came by human will, but men and women moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God.
points.apply: Keep a Bible or a Gospel book where you can see it at home, and open it once a day.

sub: Jesus reads the Psalm.
More than a king: the Son at the right hand.
The crowd listened with delight; Boniface held the Gospel to the end.
q: The Lord says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
points.apply: When you hear the Gospel at the next Holy Qurbono, listen for one word that brings you joy, and carry it with you through the day.

concl: The Scriptures we learned as children are breathed by God, and they lead us to Christ, David's son and David's Lord.
St Boniface carried them to the nations and died holding them.
2027-06-05.resolve: Read the word of God with delight, continue in what you have learned, and hand it on.

intro: Theme: “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.”
On Monday of the third week after Pentecost: holy hands lifted without anger, a Christian beauty made of good works, and the Advocate who teaches us and brings the peace of Christ.

sub: The ancient posture of prayer.
No prayer with a quarrel in our hands.
The peace passed at the Holy Qurbono.
q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
Do not worry about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
points.apply: Make it a family rule this week: no night prayer until every quarrel of the day has been made up.

sub: Beauty in deeds, not display.
Man and woman equal in dignity.
The women who teach us the faith.
q: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord is to be praised.
rather, let your adornment be the inner self with the lasting beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious in God's sight.
points.apply: Thank, in words or in writing, one woman who taught you the faith: a mother, a grandmother, a catechist or a sister.

points.h: The Advocate and the peace of Christ
sub: The Spirit teaches and reminds.
Scripture read as a whole, in the Church.
A peace the world cannot give.
q: the Lord lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth;
points.apply: Before reading a hard passage of Scripture, pray: Come, Holy Spirit, teach me; and read it with the Church's help.

concl: Prayer needs holy hands and a heart without anger; Christian beauty is made of good works.
The Holy Spirit teaches the Church to read God's word as a whole, and Christ gives the peace the world cannot give.
2027-06-07.resolve: Make peace before you pray, let the Spirit teach you, and receive the peace of Christ without fear.

intro: Theme: “You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning.”
On Tuesday of the third week after Pentecost, the memory of St Mariam Thresia: justified by faith, not building again what grace tore down, and the witness of the Spirit through our hands.

points.h: Justified through faith in Jesus Christ
sub: No one stands before God on a record of achievements.
The same grace seats everyone at one table.
Good works flow from grace; they do not buy it.
q: but the righteous live by their faith.
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
points.apply: Begin your prayer each morning this week by thanking God for one gift you did nothing to earn.

points.h: The Spirit testifies, and you also
sub: Two witnesses speaking together.
The Spirit works through our words and hands.
Witness begins with being with Jesus.
q: You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses
points.apply: Spend ten minutes with Jesus before the tabernacle or with the Gospel before you try to speak of him to anyone.

points.h: St Mariam Thresia: faith working through love
sub: A girl of Puthenchira given to prayer.
From house to house: the sick, the poor, the quarrelling.
The family as the domestic church.
q: Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
the only thing that counts is faith working through love.
points.apply: Choose one family, your own or a neighbour's, and do one concrete thing this week to bring it peace.

concl: We are made righteous by grace, not by our record, and grace makes us witnesses.
The Spirit who testified to Jesus through St Mariam Thresia wants to testify through our homes and our hands.
2027-06-08.resolve: Receive everything as gift, and let the Spirit carry Christ's love through you into one home this week.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life. Do you believe this?”
On Wednesday of the third week after Pentecost: the exchange of the Creator for creatures, a list of sins that includes us all, and Martha's faith at the tomb.

sub: Idolatry is the root.
“God gave them up”: our choices bear fruit.
Restless until the heart returns to its Maker.
q: for my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug out cisterns for themselves, cracked cisterns that can hold no water.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
points.apply: Remove or limit one thing this week that has begun to take God's place in your day.

points.h: A list that includes all of us
sub: Disorders of the body and sins of the tongue side by side.
No one may judge.
Respect, compassion and the call to conversion for all.
q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
Therefore you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge others
points.apply: For one day, say nothing about anyone who is not present, unless it is good.

points.h: “Even now”: the resurrection and the life
sub: Neighbours who come to console.
Martha's grief and faith together.
The Creator comes to the tomb.
q: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died.
points.apply: Visit or call a family that has lost someone in the past year, and pray for their departed at the next Holy Qurbono.

concl: When the Creator is exchanged for creatures, life falls into disorder; none of us is outside that story.
But the Creator has come to our tombs, and he says to every dead hope: even now.
2027-06-09.resolve: Put God back at the centre, judge no one, and answer Jesus with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe.

intro: Theme: “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.”
On Thursday of the third week after Pentecost: Epaphroditus, the co-worker who nearly died for Christ, the honour due to hidden servants, and the patient teaching of the Spirit.

sub: A messenger from Philippi.
An apostle with a small “a”.
The mission carried by unnamed hands.
q: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to do it.
esteem them very highly in love because of their work.
points.apply: Thank, by name and in person, one hidden worker of your parish this Sunday.

sub: Sickness in the service of Christ.
Paul is not ashamed of his anxiety.
Mercy spares us one sorrow after another.
q: The Lord sustains them on their sickbed; in their illness you heal all their infirmities.
the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction
points.apply: Visit or call one person who is sick, especially a health worker who has fallen ill.

sub: “You cannot bear them now.”
The Spirit takes what is Christ's.
Staying in the Spirit's school.
q: All your children shall be taught by the Lord, and great shall be the prosperity of your children.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit each day this week before you or your children begin study or work.

concl: The apostolic mission is carried by many Epaphroditus figures, and the Church must honour them.
The Spirit of truth teaches patiently, taking what is Christ's and giving it to us as we can bear it.
2027-06-10.resolve: Honour those who serve in hidden ways, and stay faithfully in the school of the Holy Spirit.

intro: Theme: “We will come to them and make our home with them.”
On the Foundation Day of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy (11 June 1932), with Mar Barthulmai and Mar Barnabas: a home given by God, the peace of the reconciled, and the faith of the apostles.

sub: The reunion at Kollam, 20 September 1930.
Christo Pastorum Principi, 11 June 1932: Thiruvananthapuram and Tiruvalla.
Not orphaned: bishops in communion with Peter's successor.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the unity of the Churches of Kerala, naming the Malankara Orthodox and Jacobite Churches with love.

sub: Justified by faith, standing in grace.
Love poured out through the Spirit.
Reconciled while we were enemies.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you
All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and has given us the ministry of reconciliation
points.apply: Take one step this week towards reconciliation with someone from whom you, or your family, have long been separated.

points.h: Mar Barthulmai: an Israelite without deceit
sub: One of the Twelve.
Nathanael under the fig tree, in the tradition.
An ancient memory of the Gospel carried to India.
q: Happy are those to whom the Lord imputes no iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no deceit.
Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!
points.apply: Be completely honest this week in one place where you have been tempted to shade the truth.

sub: A field sold for the poor.
Saul taken by the hand.
Antioch: prayer, fasting and mission.
q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were brought to the Lord.
points.apply: Encourage, in person, one newcomer, one young person and one discouraged person in your parish before the Apostles' Fast begins on Wednesday.

concl: On 11 June 1932 the Lord kept his promise not to leave his flock orphaned and gave our Church a home within the one Catholic communion.
The love poured into our hearts by the Spirit makes us reconcilers, honest like Bartholomew and encouragers like Barnabas.
2027-06-11.resolve: Love your Church as God's home, pray for her shepherds and for Christian unity, and be a Barnabas to someone this week.

intro: Theme: “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed … nothing will be impossible for you.”
On Saturday of the third week after Pentecost, on the eve of the announcement of the Apostles' Fast: Paul's heart for his people, Christ the end of the law, and the faith that prays and fasts.

sub: “My heart's desire and prayer to God for them.”
What belongs to Israel.
Reverence, not contempt.
q: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem
for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
points.apply: Pray this week for the Jewish people and for peace in the Holy Land, and refuse to repeat any joke or remark that shows contempt for any people.

points.h: Christ, the end of the law
sub: Zeal that is not enlightened.
Our own righteousness or God's?
How to keep the Apostles' Fast.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts
Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
points.apply: Before the fast begins, decide on one practice and tell no one but God about it.

points.h: Faith the size of a mustard seed
sub: A father on his knees.
“Because of your little faith.”
The faith that prays and fasts.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
points.apply: Bring one person in your family to Jesus by name every day of the Apostles' Fast.

concl: Paul teaches us to love and pray for others, and to receive righteousness from Christ rather than build our own.
A small, real faith that prays and fasts can move the mountains that weigh on our families.
2027-06-12.resolve: Name those whose salvation you desire, and begin the Apostles' Fast with humble, persevering faith.

intro: Theme: “Present your members to God as instruments of righteousness.”
On Monday of the fourth week after Pentecost, the memory of Elisha the Prophet, two days before the Apostles' Fast: a double share of the Spirit, mercy beyond borders, and bodies offered to God.

points.h: Elisha: a double share of the Spirit
sub: From the plough to the mantle.
A ministry of mercy: oil, bread, life.
A figure of Christ.
q: Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit.
The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit each morning of the Apostles' Fast for the grace you most need.

points.h: Naaman the Syrian: mercy beyond borders
sub: A widow of Sidon and a Syrian soldier.
The anger at Nazareth.
He passed through the midst of them.
q: his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
I truly understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
points.apply: Do one kindness this week for someone of another community, language or religion.

sub: Brought from death to life in Baptism.
Sin will have no dominion: grace, not law.
The Apostles' Fast: giving back our members to God.
q: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable to you, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer.
present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Write down the one offering you will make during the Apostles' Fast and place it before the image of Christ at home.

concl: Elisha's spirit, Naaman's cleansing and Paul's call all point to Christ, whose mercy reaches every nation and whose grace releases us from the rule of sin.
The Apostles' Fast is the time to offer our members to God as instruments of righteousness.
2027-06-14.resolve: Ask for a double share of the Spirit, cross one border in kindness, and choose your offering for the Apostles' Fast.

intro: Theme: “The true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth.”
On the memory of the first church built in the name of the holy Mother of God: worship in spirit and truth, the house of God, and faithfulness where we were called.

sub: Not this mountain, not that one.
The Spirit of Pentecost and Christ the Truth.
The altar at the heart of true worship.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: At the next Holy Qurbono, join your voice to the prayers and responses instead of only listening.

points.h: A house named for the Mother of God
sub: No house can contain God.
Mary, the first dwelling of the Word.
A church that points to her Son.
q: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
Surely, from now on all generations will call me blessed
points.apply: Learn the story of your parish church this week: when it was built, and why it bears its name.

points.h: Remain with God where you were called
sub: Holiness without running away.
Obeying the commandments is everything.
The house of Nazareth.
q: and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
points.apply: Choose one ordinary task you dislike and do it today carefully, as an offering to God.

concl: The first church built in the name of the Mother of God has many children, and every one of them exists for the worship the Father seeks.
Worship that begins at the altar continues in the house, the field and the classroom.
2027-06-15.resolve: Worship the Father in spirit and truth in his house, and remain with him wherever he has placed you.

intro: Theme: “It is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.”
At the beginning of the Apostles' Fast: a fast for mission, the Twelve called by name, and the trustworthy stewards of God's mysteries.

sub: Held in trust, not owned.
The priest at the altar, the parent at home.
Time, money, body and faith.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Like good stewards of the manifold grace of God, serve one another with whatever gift each of you has received.
points.apply: Make an honest list of what God has entrusted to you and choose one thing to use more faithfully during the fast.

sub: Fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot.
Mar Thoma among them.
Bishops, successors of the apostles.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles
points.apply: Pray each day of the fast for the Pope, your bishop and your parish priest by name.

sub: When the Bridegroom is taken away.
Antioch: worship, fasting, sending.
A fast without judging.
q: Yet even now, says the Lord, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
points.apply: Decide today on one fast, one daily prayer and one act of almsgiving for the whole Apostles' Fast.

concl: The Apostles' Fast is the Church's fast for mission: we deny ourselves so that the Gospel may go out.
The Twelve were stewards of the mysteries; in our measure, so are we.
2027-06-16.resolve: Keep the Apostles' Fast humbly and faithfully, praying for the successors of the apostles and judging no one before the time.

intro: Theme: “Rooted and built up in him and established in the faith.”
On Thursday of the fourth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast and the monsoon: the two builders, the fullness of Christ, and the record nailed to the cross.

sub: Both hear, both build.
The difference is underground.
Hearing is not doing.
q: Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Choose one word of Jesus you know but do not live, and act on it today.

points.h: Rooted and built up in Christ
sub: A tree and a house.
The fullness of God dwells in him.
Nothing is lacking.
q: They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream.
and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love.
points.apply: During the fast, give ten minutes each day to reading the Gospel slowly, to let your roots go deeper.

points.h: The record nailed to the cross
sub: Buried and raised in Baptism.
A bond of debt torn up.
The powers disarmed.
q: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross
points.apply: If a forgiven sin still weighs on you, bring it once more to the Lord in confession or prayer, and leave it at the cross.

concl: The floods come to every house; only the house on the rock stands.
Christ is the rock, and we build on him by doing what he says.
2027-06-17.resolve: Dig deeply in these days of fasting: hear the word of Jesus and act on it.

intro: Theme: “I do not call you servants any longer… but I have called you friends.”
On the memory of Mar Aprem Malpan, in the Apostles' Fast: the shadow and the reality, the friendship of Christ, and the Harp of the Spirit.

points.h: The shadow and the true form
sub: Sacrifices offered year after year.
What the blood of animals could not do.
The one offering of Christ.
q: Sacrifice and offering you do not desire, but you have given me an open ear.
he entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.
points.apply: At the next Holy Qurbono, unite your own small sacrifices of the fast with the one offering of Christ.

sub: The greatest love.
Knowing the Master's heart.
Chosen to bear fruit that will last.
q: Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.
