We love because he first loved us.
points.apply: Speak to Jesus today for five minutes as to a friend, telling him plainly what is in your heart.

sub: A deacon all his life.
Christ in every symbol.
Hymns that carried the faith home.
q: Awake, my soul! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awake the dawn.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; teach and admonish one another in all wisdom; and with gratitude in your hearts sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs to God.
points.apply: Learn by heart one hymn of our liturgy, or teach one to a child, this week.

concl: The shadows of the law led to Christ, and Christ leads us into friendship.
Mar Aprem sang that friendship for the whole Church; we are invited to live it and to sing it.
2027-06-18.resolve: Live as a friend of Jesus: love one another as he loved us, and praise him with your whole heart.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
On the memory of Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, in the Apostles' Fast: the body offered to do the Father's will, the second mile, and the apostle who asked a question.

points.h: See, I have come to do your will
sub: A body prepared by the Father.
From the manger to the Cross.
Our wills joined to his in the Qurbono.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work.
points.apply: Begin each day of the fast with the words: See, Lord, I have come to do your will.

sub: An eye for an eye was a limit.
Breaking the chain of revenge.
Praying for the persecutor.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Do one concrete good this week for someone who has wronged you.

points.h: Mar Yuda Thaddai: the apostle who asked
sub: Thaddaeus, Judas son of James.
How will you reveal yourself?
The helper in desperate causes.
q: Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.
But you, beloved, build yourselves up on your most holy faith; pray in the Holy Spirit; keep yourselves in the love of God
points.apply: Bring your hardest intention to the Lord today, with the prayers of St Jude, and leave it with him.

concl: The Son came to do the Father's will, and doing it led him to love his enemies to the end.
St Jude asked how Jesus would show himself; the answer is love that keeps his word.
2027-06-19.resolve: In this fast, fast from revenge: go the second mile and pray for those who hurt you.

intro: Theme: “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
On Monday of the fifth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast, with St Aloysius Gonzaga: the argument on the way, the question of whom we serve, and the young saint who chose to be last.

sub: No neutral ground.
Members given to sin or to righteousness.
Wages and gift.
q: choose this day whom you will serve
No one can serve two masters; for a slave will either hate the one and love the other, or be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
points.apply: Write down honestly where your time went yesterday, and offer tomorrow's hours to God in advance.

points.h: Last of all and servant of all
sub: The argument on the road.
The silence of the disciples.
The child in the centre.
q: The reward for humility and fear of the Lord is riches and honor and life.
Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility regard others as better than yourselves.
points.apply: Take on one humble task this week that usually falls to others, and do it without telling anyone.

points.h: St Aloysius: a young heart given whole
sub: The heir who chose another Master.
Carrying the sick in plague-stricken Rome.
Patron of students and the young.
q: Remember your creator in the days of your youth
Let no one despise your youth, but set the believers an example in speech and conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
points.apply: Pray for one young person you know who is starting a new year of study, and encourage him or her in person.

concl: Every life serves someone; only the service of God ends in eternal life.
Jesus, and St Aloysius after him, show that the greatest is the one who serves.
2027-06-21.resolve: Stop arguing about who is greatest: welcome the least, and give your members to the service of God.

intro: Theme: “The one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.”
On Tuesday of the fifth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast: almsgiving as sowing, the cheerful giver, and the treasure that lasts.

sub: Paul's collection for Jerusalem.
Seed given is not lost.
The harvest is greater than the seed.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and will be repaid in full.
give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, will be put into your lap
points.apply: Put aside what you save by fasting this week and give it before the feast of the Apostles.

sub: Not reluctantly, not under compulsion.
A heart like God's own.
The God who supplies seed to the sower.
q: Give liberally and be ungrudging when you do so, for on this account the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in all that you undertake.
remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, for he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
points.apply: The next time you give, give a little more than you planned, and give it with a smile.

sub: Moth, rust and thieves.
The poor as porters to heaven.
The Apostles who left their nets.
q: if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth,
points.apply: Name one thing you hold on to too tightly and loosen your grip on it this week.

concl: Almsgiving is not loss but sowing: what we give to God and to the poor goes ahead of us as a harvest.
The heart follows the treasure; let the fast move our treasure towards heaven.
2027-06-22.resolve: Sow bountifully, give cheerfully, and keep your treasure where moth and rust cannot reach.

intro: Theme: “Lord, I believe.”
On Wednesday of the fifth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast: Tychicus the faithful minister, the man born blind who comes to worship, and the blindness that says “We see”.

sub: Driven out by others, found by Jesus.
A seeker's honest question.
Faithful helpers like Tychicus who bring the word.
q: “Come,” my heart says, “seek his face!” Your face, Lord, do I seek.
So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
points.apply: Bring the word of God to one person who is searching, as Tychicus brought Paul's letter.

sub: From “the man called Jesus” to worship.
Baptism as illumination.
Faith that kneels.
q: O come, let us worship and bow down, let us kneel before the Lord, our Maker!
Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
points.apply: Kneel in silence for a few minutes before the tabernacle this week and renew your act of faith.

sub: The danger of the religious heart.
The doctor cannot heal one who will not be seen.
The fast as a time to admit our blindness.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped;
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
points.apply: Make a good confession before the feast of Sts Peter and Paul.

concl: Jesus seeks out the one who is driven out, and leads him from sight to faith and from faith to worship.
Only the one who admits his blindness can be given sight.
2027-06-23.resolve: Admit what you cannot see, kneel before the Lord, and say: Lord, I believe.

intro: Theme: “His name is John.”

On the Birth of John the Baptist (Yohannan Mamdana), within the Apostles' Fast, with the memory of Cheppattu Philipose Ramban: the forerunner sanctified before birth, the name given by God, the prophet who prepared the Apostles, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.

sub: Called and named before birth.
God's name over the family's custom.
The name means that the Lord has shown favour.
q: The Lord called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
points.apply: Bring one plan of yours before God this week and ask him what name he wants to write on it.

sub: Nine months of silence after doubt.
Obedience opens the lips.
The Benedictus, the morning song of the Church.
q: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them.
points.apply: Pray the canticle of Zechariah each morning until the feast of the Apostles.

sub: The hand of the Lord was with him.
The prophet of the desert and the fast.
The friend of the bridegroom who sent his disciples to the Lamb.
q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Pray by name this week for the children of your family as they begin the school year.

points.h: Holiness without which no one will see the Lord
sub: Pursue peace with everyone.
Esau's single meal and John's faithfulness.
Remembering those who spoke the word of God to us.
q: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
points.apply: Make peace with one relative, and pray for the priests and teachers who handed on the faith to you.

concl: John's birth is good news: God is gracious, and the forerunner of the Lamb has come.
Like John, we are called to holiness, to praise, and to point away from ourselves to Christ.
2027-06-24.resolve: Let God name your life, open your lips in praise, and let Christ increase in you.

intro: Theme: “Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.”

On Friday of the fifth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast: Abraham's offering, the patriarchs who blessed the generations to come, and the teaching of Jesus understood by those who do God's will.

sub: Abraham tested on the mountain.
The God who can raise the dead.
Isaac with the wood, a figure of Christ with the cross.
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.”
He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?
points.apply: Hand over to God in prayer one thing you are afraid to lose.

sub: Isaac, Jacob and Joseph at the end of life.
They did not see the promise but handed it on.
The sign of the cross on a child's forehead.
q: we will tell to the coming generation the glorious deeds of the Lord, and his might, and the wonders that he has done.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Bless the children of your home each morning this week before they leave.

sub: A teaching that comes from the Father.
Understanding is the reward of faith.
Not by appearances but by the heart.
q: for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
points.apply: Speak a kind word this week to someone you have judged by appearances.

concl: Faith trusts in the God who raises the dead, and blesses those who will come after us.
The one who does God's will comes to know the truth, and learns to see others as God sees them.
2027-06-25.resolve: Trust like Abraham, bless like Isaac and Jacob, and judge with right judgment.

intro: Theme: “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.”
On Saturday of the fifth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast, on the eve of Seminary Day: partnership in the gospel, the fragrant offering, and the children of truth.

sub: A poor church that kept on giving.
Not the gift but the fruit in the giver.
Supporting those who are formed to be sent.
q: And they came, everyone whose heart was stirred, and everyone whose spirit was willing, and brought the Lord's offering
because of your sharing in the gospel from the first day until now.
points.apply: Give generously at the Seminary Day collection and pray for vocations to the priesthood.

sub: A gift that rises like incense.
God supplies every need.
Glory to the Father for ever.
q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.
points.apply: Offer one hidden sacrifice this week for the priests of your parish.

sub: The father of lies.
Words spoken to opponents, a warning for every heart.
The fast of the tongue.
q: And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
points.apply: Pass on no message this week that you have not checked to be true.

concl: Giving to the gospel is a fragrant offering, and the God who receives it supplies every need.
The children of God listen to his word and speak the truth.
2027-06-26.resolve: Share in the gospel by your gifts, and belong to God by hearing his word and speaking the truth.

intro: Theme: “You did not choose me but I chose you.”

On Monday of the sixth week after Pentecost, the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast, with Mar Irenaeus and the name day of Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios: workers who rightly explain the word of truth, the apostolic faith handed down, the peacemaker, and the fruit that lasts.

points.h: Workers with no need to be ashamed
sub: Avoid wrangling over words.
Cutting the word of truth straight.
Every parent and catechist a worker.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
points.apply: Learn one article of the Creed well this week, so that you can explain it to a child.

points.h: Mar Irenaeus and the apostolic faith
sub: From John to Polycarp to Irenaeus.
The faith handed down openly, not secret knowledge.
The Church of Rome, founded on Peter and Paul.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
making every effort to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
points.apply: Pray tomorrow, on the feast of the Apostles, for the Pope and for the unity of all Christians.

sub: Not chosen because we were good, but to make us good.
The fruit of love that lasts.
Praying for our bishops on their name days.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness,
points.apply: Thank by name someone who handed on the faith to you.

concl: The faith of the Apostles has come to us through a chain of faithful teachers, and Irenaeus is one of its strongest links.
Christ chose us to bear the fruit that lasts: truth explained rightly and lived in love.
2027-06-28.resolve: Learn the faith, hand it on straight, avoid quarrels that wound, and bear the fruit of love.

intro: Theme: “to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message”
On the commemoration of the Twelve Apostles, the day after the feast of Sts Peter and Paul: called up the mountain, to be with him, to be sent, and having nothing yet possessing everything.

sub: Chosen after a night of prayer.
He called those whom he wanted.
Twelve foundations of a renewed people.
q: And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
points.apply: Thank God today for the moment and the people through whom he called you to faith.

sub: The first purpose of the call.
At table, on the road, at the cross.
Prayer before work.
q: One thing I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life,
I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
points.apply: Give fifteen minutes each day this week to silent prayer before the Gospel.

sub: Fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot, made one.
Thomas, who came to our land.
Bishops with the successor of Peter, and every baptized Christian.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news,
Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
points.apply: Invite one person to church or share a word of faith before the Dukhrono of St Thomas on Saturday.

sub: Now is the acceptable time.
Endurance in afflictions, hardships and hunger.
Sorrowful yet always rejoicing.
q: The Lord is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.
Then Peter said in reply, “Look, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”
points.apply: Keep one good habit from the Apostles' Fast for the rest of the year.

concl: The Twelve were called to be with Jesus and to be sent; the Church built on them is apostolic still.
Every baptized Christian shares their call: to be with the Lord, and to go where he sends.
2027-06-30.resolve: Be with Jesus each day, and go where he sends you, rich in him though having nothing.
